docs.title: 2. Release notes
docs.text:
The full list of changes is in CHANGELOG.md. Releases are annotated git tags; each tag message gives the date the milestone was completed.

Version Date Highlights Unreleased November 4, 2026 Record pages at /theses/<short id>; Cited by (OpenAlex); this manual v0.9.0 November 4, 2026 How to cite (ten CSL styles, RIS, BibTeX); Google Scholar meta tags, sitemap and canonical links; similar theses paper-v1 November 3, 2026 The version described in the research paper v0.8.0 November 2, 2026 Supervisor name variants merged for display; read-only viewer role v0.7.0 November 2, 2026 Reports per institution, by supervisor and custom, as Excel and PDF v0.6.0 November 2, 2026 Title-page rules v11; usage by country and city v0.5.0 November 2, 2026 Usage analytics without trackers; department name variants v0.4.0 November 2, 2026 Duplicate theses; browse by faculty and department v0.3.0 November 1, 2026 Metadata filling from PDFs with OCR; fields of study; quality dashboard; feeds of new additions v0.2.0 November 1, 2026 OAI-PMH data provider; CSV loader; admin panel; REST API v1; postgraduate scope v0.1.0 October 31, 2026 First public portal: harvesting from four kinds of source; Blacklight portal; backups and alerts

About the tags. The project was developed quickly (October 30 to November 4, 2026) without release tags; the milestones above were tagged retrospectively on November 4, 2026 on the commits that completed them. Commit dates were never rewritten.

Changes after paper-v1. Everything after the paper version is a post-paper change. It does not alter the results reported in the paper, which are about paper-v1 only.

Before upgrading, read the entries between your version and the new one, and chapter 4.

docs.title: 3. Installing
docs.text: This chapter installs NETD on a clean Ubuntu server. It follows what the scripts in deploy/ do on the Zambian server; where those scripts still contain the Zambian host name, the step says what to change. A container-based installer that does not assume a particular server is planned (see docs/PACKAGING-PLAN.md).

docs.title: 3.1 Prerequisites
docs.text:
Item Requirement Notes Server Ubuntu Server 24.04 or 26.04 LTS, 2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM, 20 GB free disk The Zambian installation runs on 3.8 GB RAM shared with other services; install-server.sh adds 2 GB of swap Domain name A host name pointing at the server, ports 80 and 443 open Needed for HTTPS (Let's Encrypt) Java OpenJDK 11 or later (openjdk-21-jre-headless) For Solr 9 Build tools build-essential git curl libssl-dev libyaml-dev zlib1g-dev libffi-dev libreadline-dev libsqlite3-dev sqlite3 Ruby is compiled once with ruby-build Web server Apache 2.4 with mod_proxy, mod_proxy_http, mod_headers, mod_rewrite, mod_ssl; certbot and python3-certbot-apache Apache terminates TLS and proxies to the portal OCR tesseract-ocr tesseract-ocr-eng poppler-utils For scanned theses (metadata filling) Python installed by uv (Python 3.12) No system Python packages are used Ruby 3.3.6, compiled by install-server.sh No system Ruby is used Solr 9.11 slim distribution, installed by install-server.sh Bound to 127.0.0.1:8983 Mail An SMTP account that may send (for alerts and problem reports) Optional at first; alerts are not sent without it 
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y build-essential git curl sqlite3 libsqlite3-dev libssl-dev libyaml-dev zlib1g-dev \
  libffi-dev libreadline-dev openjdk-21-jre-headless apache2 certbot python3-certbot-apache \
  tesseract-ocr tesseract-ocr-eng poppler-utils

docs.title: 3.2 Service user and code
docs.text:
Everything runs as the unprivileged user netd under /opt/netd. The repository's top-level folders (harvester/, portal/, solr/, deploy/) sit directly in /opt/netd.

sudo useradd --system --create-home --home-dir /opt/netd --shell /bin/bash netd
sudo -u netd git clone https://github.com/lightonphiri/code-datalab26-netd_aggregator.git /tmp/netd-src
sudo -u netd cp -a /tmp/netd-src/. /opt/netd/ && rm -rf /tmp/netd-src
cd /opt/netd && sudo -u netd git checkout v0.9.0      # or the latest release tag

Install uv where deploy.sh expects it:

curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sudo env UV_INSTALL_DIR=/opt/netd/bin UV_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1 sh
sudo chown -R netd:netd /opt/netd/bin

docs.title: 3.3 Swap, Solr and Ruby
docs.text:
sudo bash /opt/netd/deploy/install-server.sh

This adds a 2 GB swap file, downloads Solr into /opt/netd/solr-dist (Solr home /opt/netd/solr-home), and compiles Ruby into /opt/netd/ruby (about 15 minutes on 2 vCPU). It is safe to run again: each step is skipped when already done. RUBY_VERSION and SOLR_VERSION can be set in the environment.

docs.title: 3.4 Site-specific files (before the first deployment)
docs.text:
First create the installation's identity from an example and edit it (host name, contacts, senders, time zone; chapter 7.1):

sudo -u netd cp /opt/netd/config/examples/zambia/country.yml /opt/netd/config/country.yml
sudo -u netd nano /opt/netd/config/country.yml

The files below still carry the Zambian installation's values until the later packaging releases; change them for your host name, institutions and contacts (details in chapter 7 and chapter 8):

File Change deploy/apache/netd.conf, deploy/apache/netd-le-ssl.conf ServerName, ServerAlias, ServerAdmin, certificate paths; remove the ProxyPass … ! lines for other applications on the Zambian server (/znrp, /ojs) and the old-portal redirects if you do not need them harvester/sources.yml your repositories (one entry each) harvester/institutions.yml every institution expected to contribute, with status deploy/ops/netd-backup-to-gdrive.sh rclone remote and Drive folder for off-server backups (or disable the Drive copy)

docs.title: 3.5 Deploy
docs.text:
sudo bash /opt/netd/deploy/deploy.sh

deploy.sh creates the Solr core netd from solr/netd/conf, creates the harvester's Python environment, writes /opt/netd/portal.env with a new SECRET_KEY_BASE if it does not exist, installs the portal's gems, prepares the portal database, precompiles assets, downloads the offline place database for usage figures, installs rclone, installs and starts the systemd units, and installs the Apache sites (backing up any existing ones in /opt/netd/*.bak-*). Run it again after every code update.

docs.title: 3.6 HTTPS
docs.text:
sudo certbot certonly --webroot -w /var/www/html -d your.host.name
sudo systemctl reload apache2

Certificates renew automatically. The HTTPS site must send RequestHeader set X-Forwarded-Proto "https" (it does in deploy/apache/netd-le-ssl.conf); without it, Rails rejects form posts from the record pages.

docs.title: 3.7 Mail (optional, recommended)
docs.text:
Add the sending account to /opt/netd/portal.env (mode 600, owner netd), then restart the portal:

sudo -u netd tee -a /opt/netd/portal.env >/dev/null <<'ENV'
SMTP_ADDRESS=smtp.gmail.com
SMTP_PORT=587
SMTP_USER=sender@your.institution
SMTP_PASSWORD=app-password-for-this-service
ALERT_TO=team@your.institution
ENV
sudo systemctl restart netd-portal
sudo systemctl start netd-alert@test.service     # sends a test alert

Use one app password per service, so that one can be revoked without breaking the others.

docs.title: 3.8 First harvest
docs.text:
cd /opt/netd/harvester
sudo -u netd flock -w 7200 run.lock .venv/bin/python -m netd.cli run --full
sudo -u netd .venv/bin/python -m netd.cli report
sudo -u netd .venv/bin/python -m netd.cli check

run harvests, processes and indexes every source. A first harvest of 5,000 records takes about 15 minutes, mostly waiting for the repositories. To try one source with a few records first: netd.cli harvest --source <id> --full --limit 50, then process and index.

Metadata filling (PDF text, OCR, predictions) then runs a little every night (ml.nightly in enrichers.yml); for a large backlog see chapter 9.

docs.title: 3.9 First administrator
docs.text:
sudo bash /opt/netd/deploy/ops/netd-user.sh add EMAIL=you@your.institution NAME="Your Name"

The command prints a one-time password; the account must change it at first sign-in at /admin.

docs.title: 3.10 Checking the installation
docs.text:
Check Expected systemctl status netd-solr netd-portal both active curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3010/up HTTP 200 curl -s 'https://your.host.name/oai?verb=Identify' an OAI-PMH Identify response curl -s https://your.host.name/api/v1/stats JSON with record counts systemctl list-timers 'netd-*' harvest (daily), backup (daily), probe (every 15 minutes), weekly status sudo -u netd /opt/netd/harvester/.venv/bin/python -m netd.cli check check: OK sudo systemctl start netd-backup then tail /var/log/netd-backup.log a dated folder in /var/backups/netd/

The conformance tests in tests/ (see chapter 12) check the OAI-PMH provider and the REST API against their specifications.

docs.title: 4.1 Upgrading to a new release
docs.text:
1. Read the release notes in CHANGELOG.md for every version between yours and the new one. Changes to sources.yml, enrichers.yml or the Solr configset are listed there.
  2. Back up (the nightly backup is enough if it ran today): 
    sudo systemctl start netd-backup && tail -3 /var/log/netd-backup.log
  3. Stop the timers so that no harvest starts during the upgrade: 
    sudo systemctl stop netd-harvest.timer netd-probe.timer
  4. Get the code and keep your site-specific changes (commit them on a local branch, or keep them in files that the release does not touch, such as harvester/sources.local.yml): 
    cd /opt/netd && sudo -u netd git fetch --tags && sudo -u netd git checkout vX.Y.Z
  5. Deploy: sudo bash /opt/netd/deploy/deploy.sh (gems, database migrations, assets, Solr configset reload, systemd units, Apache sites).
  6. Rebuild derived data when the release notes say so:
  7. crosswalk, rules, exclusions or thresholds changed → netd.cli reprocess (process and index every source without harvesting, about 30 seconds per 5,000 records);
  8. Solr schema changed → netd.cli index;
  9. a model changed → netd.cli predict, then reprocess (see chapter 9; the guarded script deploy/ops/netd-ml-apply.sh does both safely). Commands that write the store run under the harvest lock: sudo -u netd flock -w 7200 run.lock .venv/bin/python -m netd.cli reprocess in /opt/netd/harvester.
  10. Start the timers and check: 
    sudo systemctl start netd-harvest.timer netd-probe.timer
sudo -u netd /opt/netd/harvester/.venv/bin/python -m netd.cli check

Rollback: check out the previous tag and run deploy.sh again. A restore of the staging store is only needed if the new release changed stored data; the backup's MANIFEST.txt gives the counts to compare.

docs.title: 4.2 Upgrading the operating system
docs.text:
NETD uses its own Ruby (compiled), its own Python (uv) and Solr's own distribution, so an Ubuntu release upgrade affects it mainly through the system libraries Ruby was linked against (OpenSSL, libffi). The scripts in deploy/ops/upgrade/ were written for the Zambian server's upgrade from 20.04 to 26.04 (November 2, 2026); the NETD-relevant ones are general:

Script Use upgrade-backup.sh full server backup before the upgrade (consistent SQLite copies, configuration, /opt), copied off the server and verified upgrade-check.sh after each release hop: services, a list of URLs, versions, netd.cli check; writes a dated report rebuild-ruby.sh rebuilds NETD's Ruby in place against the new system libraries and rebuilds native gem extensions; restores the old build if it fails compat-focal.sh only for keeping binaries built on an older release running during the upgrade (shared servers)

Checklist:

  1. Stop the NETD timers and any long-running OCR unit; timers restart after each reboot, so stop them again until the upgrade is finished.
  2. Run upgrade-backup.sh and check the copy.
  3. For each hop: apt-get -s full-upgrade (read what would be removed), full-upgrade, do-release-upgrade, reboot, upgrade-check.sh.
  4. After the last hop: rebuild-ruby.sh; recreate the harvester environment (deploy.sh does this with uv); run deploy.sh; netd.cli check.
  5. Never run apt-get autoremove without simulating it first (apt-get -s autoremove): after a release upgrade it may list packages other services need.
  6. Start the timers again.

The Zambian installation's full account of its upgrade, including what broke on the shared server, is in docs/OPERATIONS.md, "Ubuntu upgrade 20.04 → 22.04 → 24.04 → 26.04".

docs.title: 5. Using the portal
docs.text: This chapter is for readers, librarians and anyone helping others use the portal. Screenshots are from the Zambian installation (November 4, 2026).

docs.title: 5.1 Home page
docs.text: The home page has the search box, links to explore Master's and PhD theses, figures "at a glance" (theses, institutions, years covered), and the list of contributing institutions. Institutions expected to contribute but not yet harvested are listed behind a toggle with 0 records.

docs.title: 5.2 Searching
docs.text:
Type words in the search box and press Enter. The menu next to the box limits the search to Title, Author, Supervisor or Subject; the default is All fields (title, authors, supervisors, abstract, keywords, degree, faculty, department, field of study). Searching ignores accents and capitals. Quotation marks search for a phrase ("water supply").

Each result shows the title, the authors, a line with year · degree · institution, up to three lines of the abstract, and the keywords (or, when the repository gave none, the portal's field of study in italics). A Download PDF link appears when the repository gives a direct link to the full text, and Cited by N when works in OpenAlex cite the thesis (it leads to the record page's Cited by section).

  • Sort by: Best Match, Published Latest, Published Earliest, Title A-Z, Title Z-A, Newest Additions, Most Cited (most citing works in OpenAlex first).
  • Show: 10, 20, 50 or 100 results per page.
  • Duplicates: a thesis deposited more than once is listed once, under its main record.

docs.title: 5.3 Facets (filters)
docs.text:
The left-hand column narrows the results. Choose a value to filter; choose it again (or the × in the filter bar) to remove it. Several facets can be combined. A facet's "more" link opens its full list at /theses/filters/<name> (for example /theses/filters/field-of-study or /theses/filters/supervisor), sortable by count or A to Z; older /catalog/facet/<field> addresses redirect there.

Facet What it holds Institution contributing institutions (top 10, "more" for the rest) Full text whether a direct full-text link exists Citations (OpenAlex) Cited: only theses cited by at least one work in OpenAlex Degree level Masters, Doctoral, Postgraduate Diploma Research domain, Field of study, Subfield the standard OpenAlex Topics classification assigned by the portal to every thesis Faculty / School, Department from the repository's collections or the title page; spelling variants merged Programme / Discipline, Degree from the degree statement Supervisor from the repository or the thesis itself; spelling variants of one person merged Keywords (from the repository) the repository's own subject terms Year newest years first

Values the portal derived (from the collection structure, by a rule, or by a model reading the PDF) are only used in facets when their confidence is high enough; see chapter 9.

docs.title: 5.4 Browsing
docs.text: Browse in the header lists institutions, their faculties or schools, and their departments, with the number of theses in each. Each count opens the matching search.

docs.title: 5.5 Record pages
docs.text:
A record page has the address /theses/<short id> (for example /theses/unza-6330); older /catalog/<id> addresses redirect to it. It shows:

  • title, authors, abstract, degree, institution, faculty, department, supervisors, year, keywords and field of study;
  • Download PDF and Repository link (the item on the institution's repository), and view and download counts;
  • values the portal filled in itself, marked as derived, with their origin;
  • other copies of the same thesis, if any;
  • Cited by: works in OpenAlex that cite the thesis, with their year, when there are any (in the right-hand column, matched weekly; most theses have none). The section starts closed: choose + to open it and − to close it; a link to #cited-by opens it;
  • How to cite (below), Similar theses (five theses with similar titles and abstracts, closed at first like Cited by; #similar-theses opens it), a Google Scholar link, and Report a problem (a short form; reports go to the portal team).

docs.title: 5.6 How to cite
docs.text: On each record page, How to cite shows a citation in one of ten styles (APA by default; also Chicago author-date, Harvard, IEEE, MLA, Vancouver, Turabian, ACM, American Chemical Society and ABNT). Copy puts it on the clipboard; RIS and BibTeX download it for reference managers (Zotero, Mendeley, EndNote, JabRef). Titles written in capitals in the repository are put into sentence case. The link cited is the item on the institution's repository.

docs.title: 5.7 Following new additions
docs.text: Any search can be followed: Follow this search (next to the result count) gives an Atom and an RSS feed of the theses newly added to the portal that match the search and filters. Paste the feed address into a feed reader. The sort Newest Additions shows the same order on the page.

docs.title: 5.8 Metadata quality
docs.text: The public Metadata quality page shows, for the whole collection, how complete each element is and where the values come from (the repositories or the portal), against the ETD-MS 1.1 metadata standard.

docs.title: 5.9 For programs
docs.text:
• REST API (/api/v1): search, single records, institutions, statistics and bulk export (CSV, JSON Lines), with an interactive reference at /developers/api.
  • OAI-PMH (/oai): for harvesters such as NDLTD; Dublin Core and ETD-MS.

Both are described in chapter 10. The Developer Resources page on the portal links to them, and For Institutions explains how an institution's theses get into the portal.

docs.title: 6. System administration
docs.text:
Day-to-day work is done in the admin panel at /admin; server tasks use the netd.cli command line and the scripts in deploy/ops/. Command examples run on the server in /opt/netd/harvester as the netd user:

cd /opt/netd/harvester
sudo -u netd .venv/bin/python -m netd.cli <command> [options]

Any command that writes the staging store takes the harvest lock first, so it never overlaps the nightly run or a harvest started from the panel: sudo -u netd flock -w 7200 run.lock .venv/bin/python -m netd.cli <command>.

docs.title: 6.1 The admin panel
docs.text:
Page Path Who What Dashboard /admin admin each source's latest harvest, record counts, Run now; institutions not yet harvested and the weekly repository check Source /admin/sources/<id> admin runs, counts, excluded records and why Problem reports /admin/reports admin reports sent from record pages; mark resolved with a note Upload CSV /admin/csv admin check a CSV file from an institution, then load it Records /admin/records admin look up a record; correct a field; exclude or restore it Degree-level review /admin/review admin records a model thinks may be below postgraduate level Duplicates /admin/duplicates admin reject a match or choose the main record Metadata quality /admin/quality admin, viewer per-institution completeness and suggested improvements Usage /admin/usage admin, viewer searches, views, downloads, places; CSV Reports /admin/etd-reports admin, viewer reports per institution, by supervisor, custom; Excel and PDF Activity log /admin/log admin every action taken in the panel

Sessions end after 2 hours of inactivity or 12 hours in total.

docs.title: 6.2 Accounts and roles
docs.text:
Accounts are created on the server only (as root), which keeps sign-up off the public site:

bash /opt/netd/deploy/ops/netd-user.sh add EMAIL=jane@example.ac NAME="Jane Banda"            # admin; prints a one-time password
bash /opt/netd/deploy/ops/netd-user.sh add EMAIL=x@regulator.example NAME="..." ROLE=viewer   # read-only
bash /opt/netd/deploy/ops/netd-user.sh role EMAIL=... ROLE=admin|viewer
bash /opt/netd/deploy/ops/netd-user.sh reset|disable|enable EMAIL=...
bash /opt/netd/deploy/ops/netd-user.sh list

Give the one-time password to the person directly. The viewer role (for the national regulator's staff) sees reports, metadata quality and usage only.

docs.title: 6.3 Sources and institutions
docs.text:
• harvester/institutions.yml lists every institution expected to contribute, with a status (harvested, no-etds-yet, no-etd-collection, repository-unreachable, no-repository-known). Institutions not harvested appear with 0 records.
  • harvester/sources.yml lists the sources harvested (one per repository); name must equal the institution's name in institutions.yml.
  • Sources added from the panel (CSV institutions) are kept in harvester/sources.local.yml.

Adding a repository (DSpace with OAI-PMH):

  1. Check <base>/oai/request?verb=Identify and ?verb=ListSets; find the sets that hold theses.
  2. Look at a few records: ?verb=ListRecords&metadataPrefix=dim&set=<set> (degree level, PDF links).
  3. Add the source to sources.yml (see chapter 7), set the institution's status: harvested and source: <id> in institutions.yml, and deploy.
  4. flock -w 7200 run.lock .venv/bin/python -m netd.cli run --source <id> --full, then report.

Repository problems seen in practice and what to ask the institution: OAI-PMH answers noRecordsMatch or HTTP 500 while the repository shows items → the DSpace OAI index is empty: run [dspace]/bin/dspace oai import -c and schedule dspace oai import nightly; HTTP 403 or no answer from outside the campus → open the repository to the internet; theses mixed with other items → a separate theses collection.

The weekly repository check (check-repositories, Mondays) probes every institution not yet harvested and reports changes on the dashboard and in the weekly email.

Institutions without a repository send a CSV file (template at /netd-etd-template.csv, column guide on Developer Resources). In the panel: Upload CSV → choose the institution → check → load. From the shell: csv-check FILE, then a source with loader: csv and csv_path or csv_url.

docs.title: 6.4 Harvesting schedule
docs.text:
Timer When (server time, UTC) What netd-harvest.timer daily 02:30 netd.cli run (harvest, PDF text and predictions for new records, process, dedup, index), then netd.cli check netd-backup.timer daily 04:15 backup to /var/backups/netd/ and the off-server copy netd-probe.timer every 15 minutes the public site serves results netd-weekly.timer Mondays repository check and weekly status email

systemctl list-timers 'netd-*' shows the next runs. After the first harvest, runs are incremental. An unreachable repository is recorded as a failed run and does not stop the others; check then fails and an alert is sent.

docs.title: 6.5 Exclusions (postgraduate scope)
docs.text:
The portal holds postgraduate work only (scope.degree_levels in sources.yml). Records identified as below that level are left out when processing; records whose level cannot be identified are kept. To leave out one record, add it under its source with a reason:

    exclude_records:
      - oai_id: "oai:repository.example.ac:123456789/8053"
        reason: "Bachelor's dissertation in the theses collection (checked May 4, 2027)"

then process --source <id> and index (or wait for the nightly run). A model can also propose exclusions (see chapter 9); uncertain ones go to Degree-level review. The harvested record is never deleted: removing the entry brings it back. report and the source page list every exclusion.

docs.title: 6.6 Duplicates
docs.text: dedup groups theses deposited more than once: same DOI, or near-identical titles with compatible authors and years at most 2 apart. One record is the main record (an administrator's choice, else the one with a PDF, the more complete one, or the later one); the others are listed under it. It runs after every process, reprocess and run; after running it by hand, run index. Decisions in Duplicates in the panel take effect at once.

docs.title: 6.7 Corrections
docs.text:
A correction always wins over harvested, derived and predicted values, and survives later harvests. Normally use Records in the panel. From the shell:

flock -w 7200 run.lock .venv/bin/python -m netd.cli correct <record-id> supervisor "Henry J. Msango" \
    --by you@example.ac --note "from the acknowledgements"
flock -w 7200 run.lock .venv/bin/python -m netd.cli correct <record-id> _scope exclude --by ... --note ...
.venv/bin/python -m netd.cli uncorrect <record-id> <field>
flock -w 7200 run.lock .venv/bin/python -m netd.cli reprocess

Department and supervisor spelling variants are merged automatically at indexing time (see chapter 9 and chapter 7); the original spellings stay searchable and are shown on the record page.

docs.title: 6.8 Reports
docs.text: /admin/etd-reports builds reports from the search index: per institution (summary, then theses by year, degree level, year and level, type, faculty or school, faculty and department, and degree; optional usage: views and downloads, most viewed records, readers by country), by supervisor, and custom (filters, grouping by one or two fields, chosen columns, optional usage figures). Preview on screen, download as Excel or PDF (at most 1,000 rows per table in PDF).

docs.title: 6.9 Usage analytics
docs.text: The portal counts usage itself, with no third-party trackers and no IP addresses, browser details or search words kept: daily counts of searches, record views, PDF downloads (through the portal's Download links), browsing, API and OAI-PMH requests, with country and approximate city from an offline database (DB-IP Lite, refreshed monthly by deploy/ops/geoip-update.sh). Crawlers, link previews, signed-in administrators and pages after the first page of results are not counted. Treat the figures as a lower bound on use. Usage in the panel shows 7, 30, 90 or 365 days and a CSV download.

docs.title: 6.10 Backups and restore
docs.text:
deploy/ops/netd-backup.sh writes /var/backups/netd/YYYY-MM-DD/ (14 days kept) only if every step succeeds:

File Contents netd.sqlite3.gz the staging store: raw harvested XML, canonical records, predictions, corrections (the system of record) portal.sqlite3.gz portal database: accounts, activity log, problem reports, usage counts csv-sources.tgz CSV files from institutions and sources.local.yml solr-conf.tgz the Solr configset MANIFEST.txt, SHA256SUMS counts and checksums

deploy/ops/netd-backup-to-gdrive.sh copies the folder off the server with rclone and verifies every file (REMOTES lists the destinations). The Solr index is not backed up (it is rebuilt in minutes), nor is /opt/netd/portal.env (keep its values in a password manager).

Restore (after install-server.sh and deploy.sh on a new server, if needed):

D=/var/backups/netd/2027-05-04 && cd $D && sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
sudo systemctl stop netd-harvest.timer netd-portal
gunzip -c $D/netd.sqlite3.gz   | sudo -u netd tee /opt/netd/harvester/netd.sqlite3 >/dev/null
gunzip -c $D/portal.sqlite3.gz | sudo -u netd tee /opt/netd/portal/storage/production.sqlite3 >/dev/null
cd /opt/netd/harvester && sudo -u netd .venv/bin/python -m netd.cli index && sudo -u netd .venv/bin/python -m netd.cli check
sudo systemctl start netd-portal netd-harvest.timer

docs.title: 6.11 Alerts
docs.text:
Every NETD unit has OnFailure=netd-alert@%n.service, which emails the unit's status and its last 60 log lines through the SMTP account in portal.env (to ALERT_TO, else SMTP_USER). The probe alerts once per outage and once on recovery; the weekly status email confirms that the alert path works. Test it with sudo systemctl start netd-alert@test.service.

Alert First thing to do netd-harvest.service failed journalctl -u netd-harvest -n 80; PROBLEM: lines name the source; a repository that is down needs no action netd-backup.service failed tail /var/log/netd-backup.log; an authorisation error means the rclone token must be renewed netd-probe.service failed systemctl status netd-portal netd-solr apache2; restart what is down netd-solr or netd-portal failed journalctl -u <unit> -n 100, then systemctl restart <unit>

docs.title: 6.12 Command-line reference
docs.text:
Command What it does harvest [--source ids] [--full] [--limit n] harvest raw records (incremental unless --full) process [--source ids] [--db path] crosswalk, rules, overlay of predictions and corrections, scope; --db on a copy for a dry run index [--solr url] write Solr from the canonical records run [--source ids] [--full] harvest, nightly metadata filling, process, dedup, index reprocess process and index every source without harvesting report counts, completeness and exclusions per source check [--max-age-hours n] health check used after the nightly run dedup recompute duplicate groups csv-check FILE check an institution's CSV file check-repositories probe institutions not yet harvested quality-report metadata quality figures for /quality extract-text, ocr-text, text-report PDF text cache (chapter 9) predict, load-predictions, export-predictions model predictions gold-sample, evaluate [--strata] gold-standard evaluation correct, uncorrect hand corrections

Configuration paths can be overridden with environment variables (NETD_DB, NETD_SOLR, NETD_SOURCES_LOCAL, NETD_INSTITUTIONS, NETD_UPLOADS, NETD_LOGS, NETD_MODELS, NETD_OAI).

docs.title: 6.13 Rules that prevent trouble
docs.text:
• The staging store is SQLite in WAL mode: open it only as netd, never as root (a root-owned -wal or -shm file stops the harvester; fix with chown netd:netd /opt/netd/harvester/netd.sqlite3*).
  • Before a data change on the live store, dry-run on a copy: sqlite3 netd.sqlite3 ".backup /opt/netd/logs/dry.sqlite3", then process --db /opt/netd/logs/dry.sqlite3 and compare report.
  • Long jobs (OCR backlogs, full predictions) run as transient units, so a dropped SSH session does not stop them: sudo systemd-run --unit=<name> --uid=netd --gid=netd --working-directory=/opt/netd/harvester ..., followed with journalctl -u <name> -f.
  • Restarting the portal stops a harvest started from the panel; the next run finishes the job.

docs.title: 7. Configuration reference
docs.text: Every file an installation may need to change, with its settings. Paths are relative to /opt/netd (the repository root). After changing a harvester file, run reprocess (or the step named); after changing a portal or deployment file, run deploy/deploy.sh.

docs.title: 7.1 config/country.yml — the installation's identity
docs.text:
One file names the country, the portal and the people behind it. The portal, the harvester and the deployment scripts read it at start-up; a missing file, a missing required key or an unknown time zone stops them with a message that names the file and the key. Start from an example: cp config/examples/zambia/country.yml config/country.yml, then edit it and run deploy/deploy.sh. To keep the file elsewhere, set NETD_COUNTRY to its path (in portal.env and the systemd units).

country:
  name: Zambia
  adjective: Zambian
  time_zone: Africa/Lusaka          # IANA name
portal:
  name: Zambia National ETD Portal
  wordmark: [Zambia, National ETD Portal]
  host: netd.ac.zm                  # public host name, served over HTTPS
regulator:
  name: Higher Education Authority
  short_name: HEA
  url: https://www.hea.org.zm
  register_url: https://online.hea.org.zm
contact:
  email: datalab@unza.zm
  reports_to: [lighton.phiri@unza.ac.zm, datalab@unza.zm]
mail:
  from: datalab@unza.zm
  sender: lighton.phiri@unza.ac.zm
credits:
  - {name: DataLab Research Group, url: https://datalab.unza.zm, logo: datalab-logo-light.svg, logo_height: 40,
     class: datalab-credit, article: the, role: developed by}
  - {name: ZAMREN, full_name: Zambia Research and Education Network, url: https://zamren.zm, logo: zamren-logo.png,
     logo_height: 48, class: zamren-credit, role: hosted by}
citation:
  keep_capitals: [Zambia, Zambian, Zambians, Lusaka, Copperbelt, Luapula, Muchinga, Ndola, Kitwe, Kabwe, Livingstone,
                  Chipata, Kasama, Solwezi, Mongu, Mansa, Chongwe, UNZA, ZESCO, ZRA, ZNBC]
locale: en
Key Required Used for country.name, country.adjective yes page text ("theses from Zambian universities") country.time_zone yes times in the admin panel and on the quality pages, and their label ("Lusaka time") portal.name yes browser titles, the home, FAQ, About and Credits pages, e-mail, report headers and document properties, OAI-PMH Identify, RIS exports portal.wordmark yes the two parts of the header wordmark (exactly two) portal.theme no the theme folder in themes/ (colours, wordmark font, logo files; chapter 8.3); default when absent portal.host yes every absolute address: OAI-PMH base URL and identifiers (oai:<host>:<record id>), REST API links, links in e-mail, Developer Resources examples, harvester user agents, the site probe and alerts regulator.name, regulator.short_name, regulator.url yes the body that accredits the institutions: named and linked on the home, FAQ and For Institutions pages; the short name in admin pages, reports and the API's institution list ("HEA-listed"); register_url (optional) is its online register contact.email yes the public address on the pages and in OAI-PMH Identify contact.reports_to yes recipients of "Report a problem" mail.from yes default sender of portal e-mail mail.sender yes sender of problem reports when SMTP_FROM and SMTP_USER are not set in portal.env credits no developer and host credits, in order: header bar (role developed by), footer sentence and logo, About and Credits pages (role hosted by is the server's host). Each entry needs name, url, role; optional full_name, logo (file in portal/public/images/), logo_height, class (style class of the logo link), article ("the") citation.keep_capitals no your country's place names, institutions and bodies kept capitalised when a title in capitals is put into sentence case (added to a general list) locale no interface language (default en)

deploy.sh writes the values the shell scripts need to deploy/site.env (do not edit it; it is rewritten on every deployment). To see them: sudo -u netd env PYTHONPATH=/opt/netd/harvester /opt/netd/harvester/.venv/bin/python -m netd.config --env.

Changing portal.host changes the OAI-PMH identifiers of every record: harvesters of your portal will see new records. Choose the host before the portal is announced.

docs.title: 7.2 harvester/sources.yml — sources harvested
docs.text:
scope:
  degree_levels: [Doctoral, Masters, Postgraduate Diploma]   # records identified as another level are excluded

sources:
  - id: unza                       # short, lower case; used in record ids and on the command line
    name: University of Zambia     # exactly as in institutions.yml
    short_name: UNZA               # shown in results and reports
    base_url: https://rims.unza.ac.zm/server/oai/request
    formats: [dim, etdms, oai_dc]  # first one the repository offers is used
    sets: [com_123456789_18]       # OAI-PMH setSpecs holding theses
    collections_are: faculty       # repository collections name faculties (or: department)
    ignore_set_names: ["Theses and Dissertations"]   # container collections that are not units
    set_units:                     # collections that are not units: {faculty: ..., department: ...}, null for none
      col_123456789_5183: {faculty: null}
    exclude_records:               # single records left out, with the reason
      - {oai_id: "oai:rims.unza.ac.zm:123456789/8053", reason: "Bachelor of Laws dissertation"}
Key Required Meaning id, name, short_name yes identity of the source base_url OAI-PMH sources the OAI-PMH endpoint formats no metadata formats in order of preference (default [dim, etdms, oai_dc]) sets no restrict harvesting to these sets (strongly advised: repositories hold more than theses) loader no dspace7-rest (with rest_api, collections), dspace6-mets (with xmlui, collections) or csv (with csv_path or csv_url); omitted for OAI-PMH collections_are no faculty or department: map repository collection names to that unit ignore_set_names no collection names never used as units set_units no per-collection override of faculty and department exclude_records no records left out, each with oai_id and reason record_url no harvested keeps the repository's own record links; by default links are rebuilt from the OAI identifier as https://<host>/handle/<handle> files no false skips the second pass that collects direct PDF links

harvester/sources.local.yml (not in the repository) holds sources added from the admin panel, in the same format.

docs.title: 7.3 harvester/institutions.yml — institutions expected
docs.text:
institutions:
  - {name: University of Zambia, levels: [Masters, PhD], status: harvested, source: unza}
  - {name: Cavendish University, levels: [Masters, PhD], status: repository-unreachable,
     repository: "https://dspace.cavendishza.org/", oai: "...", etd_sets: [...], checked: "2026-11-01",
     note: "every path answers 403 Forbidden to outside visitors"}

status is one of harvested, no-etds-yet, no-etd-collection, repository-unreachable, no-repository-known. oai and etd_sets are probed weekly by check-repositories. In Zambia the list is every institution with an accredited Master's or Doctoral programme (from the Higher Education Authority's register); another country would use its own regulator's register.

docs.title: 7.4 harvester/enrichers.yml — cleaning and metadata filling
docs.text: Setting Default Meaning enrichers [] extra package.module:function enrichers run after the built-in rules min_confidence 0.6 values below this are searchable but not faceted ml.show_threshold 0.8 predicted values below this are not shown ml.thresholds.<field> — per-field override (field_of_study: 0.0: the model backs off to field or domain itself) ml.level_auto_exclude 0.95 a predicted below-postgraduate level at or above this excludes the record ml.level_review_min 0.6 between this and level_auto_exclude: queued for review ml.nightly true the nightly run extracts text, OCRs and predicts for new or changed records ml.nightly_pdfs, ml.nightly_ocr 300, 30 nightly limits per source (PDFs) and overall (OCR)

docs.title: 7.5 /opt/netd/portal.env — secrets and mail (not in the repository; mode 600)
docs.text:
Variable Meaning SECRET_KEY_BASE Rails secret; generated by deploy.sh SMTP_ADDRESS, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASSWORD sending account for problem reports and alerts SMTP_FROM sender address, if not SMTP_USER ALERT_TO recipients of alerts and the weekly status (default SMTP_USER) RAILS_FORCE_SSL true to have Rails itself force HTTPS (normally Apache does this) OPENALEX_API_KEY optional: the nightly Cited by job (without a key OpenAlex allows about 100 calls a day, with a free key ten times as many; on a native install the key goes in /opt/netd/openalex.env, read by systemd) and rebuilding the fields-of-study model. A key OpenAlex rejects is logged and the job runs without it

SOLR_URL is set in the systemd unit, not here.

docs.title: 7.6 systemd units — deploy/systemd/
docs.text:
Unit Notes netd-solr.service Solr on 127.0.0.1:8983, 512 MB heap netd-portal.service Puma on 127.0.0.1:3010; sets SOLR_URL, RAILS_ENV, RAILS_MAX_THREADS=3, WEB_CONCURRENCY=0; reads portal.env netd-harvest.service / .timer daily run under run.lock, then check netd-backup.service / .timer nightly backup and off-server copy; prunes search history netd-probe.service / .timer public site check every 15 minutes (address from deploy/site.env) netd-weekly.service / .timer repository check and weekly status netd-alert@.service sends the alert for a failed unit

Times in the timers are server time (UTC on the Zambian server).

docs.title: 7.7 Apache — deploy/apache/
docs.text: netd.conf (port 80: redirect to HTTPS, Let's Encrypt webroot) and netd-le-ssl.conf (port 443: TLS, RequestHeader set X-Forwarded-Proto "https", proxy / to http://127.0.0.1:3010/). Paths excluded from the proxy (ProxyPass /path !) are other applications on the same host. On a shared server, give it a catch-all default site so that unknown host names do not show another site's content.

docs.title: 7.8 Solr — solr/netd/conf
docs.text: The Blacklight schema with ASCII folding instead of ICU analysers (the slim Solr distribution has no ICU module), ETD search fields and their weights (qf, pf per search field in solrconfig.xml), spelling dictionaries, and the MoreLikeThis component used for similar theses. deploy.sh copies it into the core and reloads the core.

docs.title: 7.9 Portal
docs.text: File Setting portal/config/blacklight.yml Solr URL from SOLR_URL portal/app/controllers/catalog_controller.rb facets, search fields, sort options, results per page portal/config/publications.yml publications shown on the About page (and written to PUBLICATIONS.md by deploy/gen_publications_md.py) portal/config/csl/ citation styles and the locale file (see chapter 8) portal/app/views/static_files/robots.text.erb crawler rules (facet combinations, feeds and data formats disallowed); served at /robots.txt with the sitemap address from portal.host portal/app/views/static_files/openapi.text.erb the REST API specification, served at /api/v1/openapi.yaml with the names and addresses from config/country.yml portal/public/netd-etd-template.csv the CSV template for institutions

docs.title: 7.10 Search engines
docs.text: The sitemap is at /sitemap.xml (built from Solr, cached one day) and is named in robots.txt. Record pages carry Highwire Press citation_* meta tags (read by Google Scholar), Open Graph tags and a canonical link. To register with Google Search Console, verify the property with an HTML file in portal/public/ (keep the file, or verification is lost) and submit the sitemap. Google Scholar has no submission form; it finds records through the sitemap within weeks to months.

docs.title: 7.11 Settings still in code
docs.text:
These are planned to move into config/country.yml or templates rendered from it (docs/PACKAGING-PLAN.md):

What Where now Administrator address and host name in the Apache sites deploy/apache/ Host name in the upgrade check and the backup destination deploy/ops/upgrade/upgrade-check.sh, deploy/ops/netd-backup-to-gdrive.sh Words that are never names (title-page rules) harvester/netd/ml/models/titlepage.py

docs.title: 8. Customisation
docs.text:
How to make a NETD installation your own: its name, look, pages, language and citation styles. Start with config/country.yml (chapter 7.1): it sets the host name, contact and sender addresses, the portal name used in e-mail and reports, and the time zone. The rest of this chapter is still edits to templates and styles; the packaging plan moves them into the same file, locale files and a theme folder, release by release.

Keep your changes on a branch of your own (or in a fork) so that upgrades can be merged; after any change below, run deploy/deploy.sh.

docs.title: 8.1 Name
docs.text: Where it appears File Browser titles and Blacklight's own labels, OAI-PMH Identify repository name, RIS exports portal.name in config/country.yml Header wordmark (two parts, e.g. "Zambia" and "National ETD Portal") portal.wordmark in config/country.yml Footer credit line, header group bar credits in config/country.yml (sentence built in portal/app/views/shared/_footer.html.erb) Home page introduction portal.name, country.adjective and regulator in config/country.yml; the rest of the text in portal/app/views/catalog/_home_text.html.erb Emails (problem reports, alerts), Excel and PDF reports, OAI-PMH administrator e-mail portal.name, portal.host, contact.email in config/country.yml REST API specification portal.name, portal.host, country.adjective, regulator.name, contact.email and the developed by credit in config/country.yml; the rest in portal/app/views/static_files/openapi.text.erb

docs.title: 8.2 Logo and credits
docs.text: Credits are listed in credits in config/country.yml (chapter 7.1): the header bar and footer name the entry with role developed by, and the About and Credits pages show every entry's logo, in order; an entry without logo, or whose file is not found, is shown by its name instead (and the footer then shows no logo). Put the logo files in your theme's public/images/ folder (section 8.3; for example themes/zambia/public/images/) and name them in logo (with logo_height in pixels); they are served at /images/<file>. class is the style class of the logo link (datalab-credit and zamren-credit are styled in netd.css). The site icons are part of the theme as well (section 8.3).

docs.title: 8.3 Colours and fonts
docs.text:
Colours, the wordmark font and the logo files form a theme: a folder themes/<name>/ named by portal.theme in config/country.yml (chapter 7.1). Two are shipped: zambia (navy and blue, Cinzel wordmark, the DataLab and ZAMREN logos) and default (neutral slate and blue, the system serif font, a neutral book icon, no logos), used when portal.theme is not set. To make your own, copy themes/default to themes/<name>, edit it and set portal.theme: <name>; then run deploy/deploy.sh (it rebuilds the style sheets) or restart the portal.

themes/<name>/
  stylesheets/theme.css    colours and fonts (below)
  public/images/           logo files named in credits; served at /images/<file>
  public/icon.png          site icon, 512 x 512 pixels (home-screen and app icon)
  public/icon.svg          the same icon as SVG
  public/favicon.svg       optional browser-tab icon (or favicon.ico); without it the pages use Blacklight's

The two shipped themes, on the home page and the Credits page. default is shown with the Zambian credits, whose logo files it does not have, so the Credits page names them instead:

zambia default

theme.css sets CSS variables that portal/app/assets/stylesheets/netd.css (the layout) reads:

:root {
  --netd-navy: #2f3a45;           /* group bar, first wordmark part */
  --netd-blue: #2b6cb0;           /* links, buttons, second wordmark part */
  --netd-blue-dark: #22558a;      /* hover */
  --netd-blue-pale: #eef3f9;      /* menu hover background */
  --netd-wordmark-rule: #b5c3d1;  /* line between the wordmark parts */
  --netd-wordmark-font: Georgia, "Times New Roman", serif;
  --netd-muted: #5b6470;          /* secondary text */
  --netd-line: #e3e6ea;           /* rules and borders */
  --bs-primary: #2b6cb0;          /* Bootstrap's own variables repeat the blue */
  --bs-primary-rgb: 43, 108, 176;
}

Change the variables rather than individual rules; the -rgb triplets must match the colour above them. A web font is loaded with an @import at the top of theme.css (the zambia theme loads Cinzel). theme.css is read after netd.css, so it may also override a rule. Check contrast for text on the header colour (at least 4.5:1).

docs.title: 8.4 Static pages
docs.text:
Page Template About (project, team, publications) portal/app/views/pages/about.html.erb and portal/config/publications.yml FAQ pages/faq.html.erb Developer Resources pages/developers.html.erb; API reference pages/api_docs.html.erb For Institutions (how to contribute) pages/contribute.html.erb Credits pages/credits.html.erb Metadata quality (public) portal/app/views/quality/index.html.erb

The templates hold the layout; the wording of these pages (except the quality page) is in portal/config/locales/en.yml under netd.about, netd.faq, netd.developers, netd.api_docs, netd.contribute and netd.credits (section 8.6). To add a question to the FAQ, add an <h2> and a <p> to the template, each with an nt(...) call, and their two keys to en.yml.

The FAQ describes what is counted in usage analytics and how long server logs are kept (netd.faq.no_the_portal_uses_html); update it to match your server and your country's data protection law.

docs.title: 8.5 Facets, fields and sorting
docs.text: Facets, search fields, sort options and results per page are set in portal/app/controllers/catalog_controller.rb (add_facet_field, add_search_field, add_sort_field). Search field weights are in solr/netd/conf/solrconfig.xml. A new facet needs a Solr field written by harvester/netd/index.py.

docs.title: 8.6 Languages
docs.text:
The interface is in English. Its wording is being moved out of the templates into portal/config/locales/en.yml, a few pages per release: the header, footer, home page, the static pages (About, Credits, FAQ, For Institutions, Developer Resources, REST API reference), Browse by Faculty, Follow a search, Metadata Quality, the record page (netd.record, including the Report a problem form) and the search result cards (netd.results) are there now, under netd.header, netd.footer, netd.home, netd.about and so on; the institution statuses (netd.institution_status) and the quality groups (netd.quality_groups) too; the admin navigation, the sign-in, password, activity log, level review, problem report and CSV upload pages (netd.admin) and the mail sent to the team for a problem report (netd.mail.problem, plain text: keep the spaces that line up its labels) as well; the remaining admin pages (dashboard, source, record correction, duplicates, quality, usage, the report forms), the kinds of use counted (netd.usage_events) and the messages shown after an action (netd.flash) too, so every page's own text is in this file. What stays in the code: the contents of the reports for the regulator (titles, headings and notes of the Excel, PDF and preview tables), the problem types offered by the Report a problem form (they are stored with each report, so changing them needs a data migration), validation messages from the models, and the field names on the record correction page. In development and test a missing key raises an error (config.i18n.raise_on_missing_translations), so a typing error in a key shows at once; in production a key missing from a translation falls back to English. The names of the facets, of the fields in a search, and of the sort options are Blacklight's own keys, below the netd: block in the same file: blacklight.search.fields.facet.<field>, ...search.<field> and ...sort.<option> (for example blacklight.search.fields.facet.institution_ssim: "Institution"). Dates use the formats time.formats.netd and date.formats.netd ("November 5, 2026"); a translation with Rails' month names for its language (the rails-i18n gem, or date.month_names in its own file) prints them in that language. Each heading, paragraph, list item and table cell is one key, named after its first words; page_title is the browser tab title and heading_html the page heading. Blacklight's own texts (search form, pagination, facet buttons) come from the Blacklight gem, and the portal name from config/country.yml through portal/config/locales/netd_country.rb.

To change a sentence, edit its key in en.yml and restart the portal (sudo systemctl restart netd-portal). Names come from config/country.yml: write %{portal}, %{country}, %{country_adjective}, %{regulator}, %{regulator_short}, %{email}, %{host} or %{base_url} rather than the name or address itself, so the text stays right for another installation. A count with singular and plural forms has one: and other: below its key (for example netd.browse.departments); languages with more plural forms add them the same way. Keys ending in _html may contain HTML (write & as &); the comments in the file say which keys take extra values such as %{n} or %{link}.

To add a language, copy en.yml to, for example, fr.yml, change the first line to fr: and translate the values (keep the keys and the %{...} names), translate Blacklight's texts the same way (blacklight.fr.yml, from the gem's own file), and set the locale in portal/config/application.rb (config.i18n.default_locale = :fr). Metadata is shown in the language it was deposited in.

docs.title: 8.7 Citation styles
docs.text:
"How to cite" uses official Citation Style Language files in portal/config/csl/, rendered by citeproc-ruby; terms come from locales-en-GB.xml. To add a style, copy an independent .csl file from https://github.com/citation-style-language/styles into that folder and add a line to Citation::STYLES in portal/app/models/citation.rb (key, label, file name). To change the default, set Citation::DEFAULT. For another language's terms, add its locale file from https://github.com/citation-style-language/locales.

Titles written in capitals are put into sentence case; words that must keep their capital letter are a general list (KEEP_GENERAL in citation.rb: continents, directions, diseases, international bodies, Roman numerals) plus citation.keep_capitals in config/country.yml. Add your country's place names, institutions and bodies there.

docs.title: 8.8 Time zone and dates
docs.text: Dates are written as "January 3, 2027". Admin panel and quality-page times are shown in country.time_zone from config/country.yml (labelled with its city, e.g. "Lusaka time"); stored and API times are UTC; systemd timers run in the server's time zone.

docs.title: 9. Metadata filling
docs.text: Repository metadata is often missing the fields readers and regulators want most: supervisor, department, faculty, degree and level. NETD fills them from the theses themselves, marks every filled value as derived, and only shows values its models are confident about. A runnable, step-by-step explanation is in notebooks/netd26-03-ml_metadata_filling-walkthrough.ipynb.

docs.title: 9.1 How it works
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  R[(canonical records)] -->|PDF links| T[extract-text<br/>ocr-text]
  T --> PT[(PDF text cache)]
  PT --> P[predict]
  R -->|harvested values only| P
  P --> PR[(prediction cache)]
  J[JSON Lines from<br/>elsewhere] -->|load-predictions| PR
  A[admin panel or<br/>netd.cli correct] --> C[(corrections)]
  PR --> O[overlay during process]
  C --> O
  O --> R2[record shown<br/>value, origin, confidence]
  1. Text cache. extract-text downloads each record's front-matter PDFs (title page and similar first, at most three files, at most 60 MB each) and keeps the text of the first 8 pages. PDFs without a text layer are OCRed by ocr-text (Tesseract, first 5 pages, about 20 seconds each, at low priority).
  2. Predictions. predict runs every model over the PDF text and the record's harvested values (never other models' output, so results do not feed back on themselves). A model runs again for a record only when its input or its version changes. Each prediction has values, a confidence and evidence (the text it came from).
  3. Overlay. During process, an empty field takes the best prediction whose confidence reaches the threshold (ml.show_threshold, 0.8). The value is marked model:<name>-<version> with its confidence, shown as derived on the record page and in the API. A hand correction always wins.
  4. Scope. A model's prediction that a record is below postgraduate level excludes it at confidence 0.95 or more (ml.level_auto_exclude), or queues it for review between 0.6 and 0.95.

The nightly run does steps 1 and 2 for new or changed records (limits in enrichers.yml), so new theses get derived values the same night.

docs.title: 9.2 Models included
docs.text:
Model Fields Method titlepage-rules (v11) degree, discipline, degree level, faculty, department, supervisors rules over title-page, approval-page and acknowledgement text: degree statements ("in partial fulfilment of the requirements for the degree of …"), unit lines, supervisor statements in many forms, name clean-up openalex-fos research domain, field of study, subfield (OpenAlex Topics) title and abstract → MiniLM sentence embedding (fastembed, CPU) → logistic regression over 252 OpenAlex subfields, backing off to field or domain when uncertain

Limits. titlepage-rules was developed and tuned on title pages from the University of Zambia and checked on three other Zambian institutions. Other institutions' title pages, other languages and other degree wording will need new rules or a new model; measure before trusting it (9.4). The words it treats as never being names include Zambian institution abbreviations (NOT_NAMES in titlepage.py). OCR quality limits what can be read from older scanned theses.

docs.title: 9.3 Thresholds
docs.text: Set in harvester/enrichers.yml under ml (see chapter 7). Raising show_threshold shows fewer, more reliable values; lowering it fills more fields with more errors. After changing a threshold, run reprocess; predictions do not need to be recomputed.

docs.title: 9.4 Evaluating with a gold standard
docs.text:
Never change a threshold or a model without measuring it on hand-checked records.

  1. gold-sample /opt/netd/logs/gold.csv --n 300 writes a sample stratified by institution (duplicate copies left out) with harvested values, empty gold_* columns, and a dev/test half for each record.
  2. Annotators fill the gold_* columns from the PDFs (several values separated by ||; - when the thesis does not say).
  3. evaluate gold.csv prints coverage, precision, recall and F1 per model, version and field at thresholds 0, 0.8 and 0.95; --strata splits the figures by kind of PDF text (born-digital, scanned and OCRed, scanned and waiting, no text).
  4. Tune on the dev half only; report the test half. People are matched by surname with compatible initials.

docs.title: 9.5 Running a backlog
docs.text:
For a first installation, or after a repository outage, run text extraction and OCR as a transient unit in batches under the harvest lock, so the nightly run waits at most one batch:

sudo systemd-run --unit=netd-mltext --uid=netd --gid=netd --working-directory=/opt/netd/harvester --nice=10 \
  /bin/bash -c 'for i in $(seq 1 15); do flock -w 7200 run.lock .venv/bin/python -m netd.cli extract-text --limit 500 || exit 1; done;
                for i in $(seq 1 80); do flock -w 7200 run.lock .venv/bin/python -m netd.cli ocr-text --limit 50 || exit 1; done'
journalctl -u netd-mltext -f

Then predict and apply safely: sudo systemd-run --unit=netd-mlapply --uid=netd --gid=netd /opt/netd/deploy/ops/netd-ml-apply.sh runs predict, a dry run on a copy of the store, and reprocess only if the dry run would exclude at most 10 new records on a model's say. deploy/ops/ocr-resume.sh keeps OCRing while a repository answers and waits while it does not.

docs.title: 9.6 Adding a model
docs.text:
A model is a Python module with:

NAME = "my-model"           # used in provenance: model:my-model-<VERSION>
VERSION = "1"               # change it whenever the output can change
FIELDS = ["supervisor"]     # fields it predicts
USES = ["title", "degree"]  # harvested fields it reads

def predict(record, text):
    """record: harvested values of USES; text: cached PDF text (pages).
    Returns {field: (values, confidence, evidence)}."""
    return {"supervisor": (["Jane Banda"], 0.9, "Supervisor: Prof. Jane Banda")}

Register it in MODELS in harvester/netd/ml/predict.py, then predict --model my-model, evaluate on the gold standard, and reprocess when the figures are acceptable. Predictions made elsewhere (a notebook with a GPU, an external service) can be loaded instead: JSON Lines with record_id, field, model, version, value, confidence (optional evidence, input_hash), then load-predictions FILE.jsonl and reprocess.

Simpler clean-ups that need no PDF text can be enrichers: a function enrich(record) -> record registered in enrichers.yml as package.module:function, which sets record["provenance"][field] and optionally record["confidence"][field] for every value it changes.

docs.title: 9.7 Name variants (display only)
docs.text: At indexing time, spelling variants of department names (harvester/netd/units.py) and of supervisor names (harvester/netd/people.py) are merged per institution. The store and the predictions are not changed; the original spellings remain searchable and are shown on the record page. Supervisor spellings join only when the surname matches and the initials agree; bare surnames never join. Department merges by edit distance are tuned with FUZZY_RATIO and FUZZY_MAX in units.py.

docs.title: 10. Interfaces
docs.text: NETD offers its collection to programs through four interfaces. All of them read the Solr index only, so they show what the nightly index holds and never touch the staging store. Examples use the Zambian installation, https://netd.ac.zm.

docs.title: 10.1 REST API v1
docs.text:
Base address /api/v1. Read-only JSON, no authentication, CORS open. The contract is /api/v1/openapi.yaml (OpenAPI 3.0.3, rendered from portal/app/views/static_files/openapi.text.erb with the installation's names and addresses), rendered with an interactive reference at /developers/api.

Endpoint What GET /api/v1/records search: q, filters (institution, degree level, year range, field of study, cited=true or false, and more), sort (relevance, newest, cited and others), page, per_page (up to 10,000 results in all) GET /api/v1/records/{id} one record (full id, or the short id of its page address) GET /api/v1/institutions every institution expected, with record counts, harvest status and last run GET /api/v1/stats counts by institution, level and year, and completeness per field (cached 10 minutes) GET /api/v1/export.csv, /api/v1/export.jsonl the whole collection (rebuilt when more than 6 hours old) 
curl -s 'https://netd.ac.zm/api/v1/records?q=malaria&per_page=5' | python3 -m json.tool

Each record has stable public field names (title, authors, supervisors, degree, degree_level, institution {id, name}, fields_of_study, links {portal, source, pdf, api}, files, duplicate_of, other_copies, openalex_id, cited_by {count, works}, updated_at) and a derived list naming every value the portal filled in, with its method and confidence. Lists are always arrays; missing single values are null. cited_by.count is null when the thesis has not been matched in OpenAlex (not yet checked, or no confident match) and 0 when it was matched and nobody cites it; each citing work has openalex_id, title, year, type and url. The CSV export ends with the columns openalex_id and cited_by_count (API 1.7.0).

Limits: 120 requests a minute per address, 20 an hour for the export. Errors: 400 with a message for bad parameters, 404, 503 when the index is unavailable.

Versioning: within v1, fields are only added, never renamed or removed (the minor version in the specification records each addition). An incompatible change would be /api/v2, with v1 kept for at least 6 months.

docs.title: 10.2 OAI-PMH data provider
docs.text:
Base address /oai (OAI-PMH 2.0), for aggregators such as NDLTD's Global ETD Search.

Aspect Value Verbs all six, GET or POST Formats oai_dc; etdms (ETD-MS v1.1, supervisors as contributor role="advisor", degree with name, level, discipline and grantor) Sets inst:<source id> per institution; level:masters, level:doctoral, level:postgraduate-diploma Identifiers oai:<host>:<record id>; in the records, dc:identifier (oai_dc) and identifier (ETD-MS) list the portal page, the repository page, the PDF and, when matched, the thesis in OpenAlex (https://openalex.org/W…) Datestamps when the record's content last changed in the portal (seconds granularity), so incremental harvesting only returns real changes Paging 100 records per page; stateless resumption tokens valid 24 hours Deleted records transient 
curl -s 'https://netd.ac.zm/oai?verb=ListRecords&metadataPrefix=etdms&set=level:doctoral'

tests/oai_conformance.py validates an installation against the OAI-PMH and Dublin Core schemas and exercises every verb and error.

docs.title: 10.3 Sitemap and search engine tags
docs.text: /sitemap.xml lists every record page (rebuilt from Solr, cached one day). Record pages carry Highwire Press citation_* meta tags (title, authors, date, institution as dissertation institution, PDF link), Open Graph tags and a canonical link, which is what Google Scholar reads. See chapter 7, 7.9.

docs.title: 10.4 Feeds
docs.text: /follow with any search's parameters gives Atom and RSS feeds of new additions matching that search, dated by the day each thesis was added to the portal. The search results page links to them ("Follow this search"). Crawlers are asked not to fetch feeds (robots.txt).

docs.title: 10.5 Other
docs.text:
• Blacklight's own JSON view of search pages (/catalog.json?q=...) follows the website and may change; use the REST API instead.
  • /up returns HTTP 200 when the portal is running (for uptime monitors).
  • The CSV template for institutions is at /netd-etd-template.csv.

docs.title: 11. Architecture and directory layout
docs.text: This chapter summarises the design. The full design, with UML views and the rationale for each decision, is docs/SDD.md (IEEE 1016); the requirements are docs/SRS.md (ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148).

docs.title: 11.1 Components
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  subgraph harvester ["harvester/ (Python)"]
    CLI[netd.cli] --> HV[harvest, rest, mets, csvload]
    CLI --> CW[crosswalk + enrich]
    CLI --> ML[ml: textcache, predict, overlay, evaluate]
    CLI --> DD[dedup]
    CLI --> IX[index + units + people]
    HV --> ST[(netd.sqlite3)]
    CW --> ST
    ML --> ST
    DD --> ST
  end
  IX --> SOLR[(Solr core netd)]
  subgraph portal ["portal/ (Rails 8 + Blacklight 9)"]
    CAT[CatalogController<br/>search, records, cite, sitemap]
    OAI[OaiController]
    API[Api::V1 controllers]
    ADM[Admin controllers]
    PDB[(production.sqlite3)]
  end
  CAT --> SOLR
  OAI --> SOLR
  API --> SOLR
  ADM --> SOLR
  ADM --> PDB
  ADM -->|reads, runs netd.cli| ST
  AP[Apache: TLS, proxy] --> portal
Component Responsibility netd.harvest OAI-PMH client (Sickle): format choice, sets, incremental runs, retries, run log; second pass for PDF links (ore) netd.rest, netd.mets, netd.csvload fallback loaders: DSpace 7 REST, DSpace 6 METS exports, CSV files; all write DSpace dim XML to the raw layer netd.store SQLite store: raw layer (XML as received), canonical layer, harvest runs, set names, predictions, corrections, duplicates netd.crosswalk dim/etdms/oai_dc → canonical record; units from collections; record links; provenance netd.enrich built-in cleaning rules and plug-in enrichers netd.ml PDF text cache and OCR, models, prediction cache, overlay, evaluation netd.dedup duplicate groups and main records netd.index, netd.units, netd.people Solr documents; department and supervisor variants merged for display netd.quality, netd.repocheck metadata quality figures; weekly check of repositories not yet harvested Portal Blacklight search and record pages, browse, citations, feeds, sitemap, OAI-PMH provider, REST API, admin panel, reports, usage counting

docs.title: 11.2 Data
docs.text:
• Staging store harvester/netd.sqlite3 (SQLite, WAL mode): the system of record. The raw layer is never changed by processing, so the canonical layer can always be rebuilt (reprocess).
  • Canonical record: ETD-MS-shaped fields (title, authors, supervisors, degree, discipline, level, grantor, faculty, department, date, abstract, subjects, links, files), each value with its provenance (harvested, set:<spec>, rule:<name>, text:<rule>, model:<name>-<version>, corrected:<by>) and, for derived values, a confidence.
  • Search index: Solr core netd with Blacklight's dynamic-field naming (*_ssim, *_tsim, *_isi, *_dtsi); rebuilt from the store in minutes, so not backed up.
  • Portal database portal/storage/production.sqlite3: accounts and sessions, activity log, problem reports, usage counts (aggregate only), search history (one day).

docs.title: 11.3 Deployment
docs.text: One server, no containers: Apache (TLS, reverse proxy) → Puma (127.0.0.1:3010) → Solr (127.0.0.1:8983). All NETD services run as the unprivileged user netd under /opt/netd, managed by systemd units with failure alerts. Python comes from uv, Ruby is compiled once, Solr is the upstream distribution, so the operating system's own packages are hardly touched (the design suits a shared server with 4 GB of memory). The choice of a custom pipeline with Blacklight over InvenioRDM, VuFind or DSpace-as-aggregator, of SQLite over PostgreSQL, and of native services over Docker, is explained in SDD section 9.

docs.title: 11.4 Directory layout
docs.text: Path Contents harvester/netd/ the Python package (modules above); ml/models/ the models and their data harvester/sources.yml, institutions.yml, enrichers.yml configuration (chapter 7) harvester/tools/ training scripts for the fields-of-study model portal/app/controllers/ catalog, browse, follow, pages, quality, OAI, problem reports; api/v1/; admin/ portal/app/components/ header, result card, record page, facet components portal/app/models/ Citation, ApiRecord, InstitutionRegistry, Harvester, QualityReport, GeoLookup, User, usage models portal/app/reports/ report definitions (hea_report.rb) and the Excel and PDF renderers portal/app/views/ templates (pages, catalog, admin, mailers) portal/config/ Blacklight, routes, locales, citation styles (csl/), publications portal/public/ static files: API specification, CSV template, images, robots.txt solr/netd/conf/ Solr configset deploy/ install-server.sh, deploy.sh, apache/, systemd/, ops/ (backup, alert, probe, users, ML apply, OCR resume, GeoIP update, upgrade/) tests/ OAI-PMH and REST API conformance tests; unit tests notebooks/ metadata-filling walkthrough docs/ SRS, SDD, this manual, the Zambian operations runbook, plans and backlog

docs.title: 12.1 Local set-up
docs.text:
You need Python 3.12 (with uv or venv), Ruby 3.3 with Bundler, Java 11 or later, and a Solr 9 core made from solr/netd/conf.

Solr:

curl -fsSLO https://dlcdn.apache.org/solr/solr/9.11.0/solr-9.11.0-slim.tgz && tar xzf solr-9.11.0-slim.tgz
mkdir -p solr-home/netd && cp solr-9.11.0-slim/server/solr/solr.xml solr-home/
cp -r solr/netd/conf solr-home/netd/conf && echo "name=netd" > solr-home/netd/core.properties
solr-9.11.0-slim/bin/solr start -p 8983 -s "$PWD/solr-home"

Harvester (a small sample from one repository):

cd harvester
uv venv --python 3.12 .venv && uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -r requirements.txt
.venv/bin/python -m netd.cli harvest --source unza --full --limit 50
.venv/bin/python -m netd.cli process
.venv/bin/python -m netd.cli report
NETD_SOLR=http://127.0.0.1:8983/solr/netd .venv/bin/python -m netd.cli index

Portal:

cd portal
bundle install
bin/rails db:prepare
SOLR_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8983/solr/netd bin/rails server     # http://127.0.0.1:3000

Create an admin account for local work with the rake task behind deploy/ops/netd-user.sh (portal/lib/tasks/netd_users.rake).

docs.title: 12.2 Tests
docs.text:
Test Run Checks tests/test_people.py python3 -I tests/test_people.py supervisor name merging (FR-64) tests/oai_conformance.py python tests/oai_conformance.py [BASE_URL] the OAI-PMH provider against the schemas, every verb and error (about five minutes on 5,000 records) tests/api_conformance.py python tests/api_conformance.py [BASE] every REST API endpoint against the OpenAPI specification netd.cli evaluate see chapter 9 model quality on a gold standard netd.cli check on any installation sources fresh, index in step with the store, OAI-PMH answering

When testing a live installation, add check to the user agent (for example Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) Firefox/140.0 netd-check) so that test requests are not counted as usage.

docs.title: 12.3 How changes are made
docs.text:
1. Requirements first. Every feature or behaviour change updates docs/SRS.md (a requirement with an identifier, and the revision history) and docs/SDD.md (the design and the revision history) in the same change. Both are published in this site under Reference (requirements, design) each time it is built.
  2. Data changes are dry-run on a copy of the store before they reach the live one; model changes are tuned on the dev half of the gold standard and reported on the test half.
  3. Small releases. Each release is one commit (or a few) that can be deployed and checked on its own.
  4. Changelog and tags. Add the change under [Unreleased] in CHANGELOG.md. A release moves those entries under a new version heading and gets an annotated tag vX.Y.Z on its commit (Semantic Versioning: a new feature raises Y, a fix raises Z). Commit dates and published tags are never rewritten.
  5. Documentation. User-visible changes update this manual; installation-specific operations go in the installation's own runbook (for Zambia, docs/OPERATIONS.md).

docs.title: 12.4 Conventions
docs.text:
• Provenance on every value. Code that sets or changes a field records how (record["provenance"][field]) and, when derived, how sure (record["confidence"][field]). Never overwrite harvested data in the raw layer.
  • Models see harvested values only and carry a VERSION that changes whenever their output can change.
  • Store access: the SQLite store is in WAL mode; read everything you need first, then write (never keep a read cursor open while writing in the same connection); only the netd user opens it.
  • No new services without a strong reason: the design fits a shared server with 4 GB of memory.
  • Interfaces are contracts: REST API v1 fields are only added; OAI-PMH output follows the schemas (run the conformance tests).
  • Language and dates: British English in code comments, documents and the interface; dates written as "January 3, 2027".
  • Privacy: usage counting keeps no IP addresses, browser details or search words; keep it that way.

docs.title: 1.1 Purpose
docs.text: This document specifies the requirements for a national Electronic Theses and Dissertations (ETD) aggregation service for Zambia. The service harvests ETD metadata from Higher Education Institution (HEI) institutional repositories (IRs) using OAI-PMH, cleans and enriches it, and offers faceted discovery by Title, Author, Subject, Supervisor, Faculty and Department. It is intended for the DataLab project team, HEI repository managers, and reviewers such as the Higher Education Authority (HEA).

docs.title: 1.2 Scope
docs.text:
The system ("NETD v2") replaces, in stages, the current Zambia National ETD Portal at https://netd.ac.zm, which runs the UCT ETD Portal software [R4] and holds about 5,269 UNZA records [R1]. Since October 31, 2026 (v0.8) it is served at https://netd.ac.zm/, replacing the earlier portal, and covers:

  • harvesting from four HEIs (UNZA RIMS and UNILUS over OAI-PMH; ZCAS University over the DSpace REST API; Mulungushi University from DSpace 6 METS exports), and listing all HEA-accredited postgraduate institutions [R12], [R13];
  • a cleaning pipeline with a plug-in point for DataLab's machine-learning (ML) models;
  • a Blacklight 9 discovery interface over Apache Solr.

Out of scope: depositing ETDs, user accounts and hosting full texts. (Replacing the earlier portal was completed in v0.8.)

docs.title: 1.3 Definitions, acronyms and abbreviations
docs.text: Term Meaning ETD Electronic Thesis or Dissertation HEI Higher Education Institution IR Institutional Repository (e.g. DSpace) OAI-PMH Open Archives Initiative Protocol for Metadata Harvesting, v2.0 oai_dc, dim, etdms OAI-PMH metadata formats: unqualified Dublin Core; DSpace Intermediate Metadata; ETD-MS ETD-MS NDLTD's interoperability metadata standard for ETDs (v1.1) Raw store Unmodified harvested metadata, kept so cleaning can be re-run Canonical record Cleaned ETD record with per-field provenance Provenance The origin of a field value: harvested, derived from sets, extracted from text, or produced by a model Enricher A cleaning/enrichment function, rule-based or ML, run on canonical records
