docs.title: 1.5 Overview
docs.text: Section 2 describes the product context and constraints. Section 3 lists verifiable requirements. Section 4 gives verification methods and traceability.

docs.title: 2.1 Product perspective
docs.text:
NETD v2 follows the SA NETD multi-tier model [R4]: Harvester → Repository (store) → Portal. It adds a cleaning tier with provenance between harvesting and indexing, motivated by the metadata-quality findings in [R2], [R5] and [R6]. Downstream, it exposes its own OAI-PMH data provider (https://netd.ac.zm/oai, EI-4) so that NDLTD [R9] and other aggregators can harvest Zambia as a single source.

flowchart LR
  subgraph HEIs
    A[UNZA RIMS<br/>DSpace 7+] ; B[UNILUS<br/>DSpace 7+] ; C[Other HEI IRs]
  end
  A & B & C -- OAI-PMH --> H[Harvester]
  H --> R[(Raw store)]
  R --> P[Crosswalk + Enrichers<br/>rules & ML models]
  P --> K[(Canonical records<br/>with provenance)]
  K --> S[(Solr index)]
  S --> U[Blacklight portal<br/>netd.ac.zm]
  K --> O[OAI-PMH provider /oai] --> N[NDLTD Union Catalog]

docs.title: 2.2 Product functions (summary)
docs.text:
1. Register and onboard HEI repositories (source registry).
  2. Harvest ETD metadata selectively (by set) and incrementally.
  3. Keep raw metadata unchanged, and process it into canonical records.
  4. Clean and enrich fields with rules and pluggable ML models, recording provenance.
  5. Index records and offer search, faceting, sorting and record pages.
  6. Report field completeness per institution.

docs.title: 2.3 User classes and characteristics
docs.text: User class Description Main needs Researcher / student (public) Searches for ETDs nationally Fast search; facets by institution, faculty, department, supervisor, subject, year; link to full text HEI repository manager Librarian responsible for an IR Confirm their ETDs are harvested; see completeness gaps Portal administrator (DataLab) Runs the service; signs in to the admin panel (FR-36 to FR-41) Add sources, run harvests, load CSV files, handle problem reports, monitor Data scientist (DataLab) Builds cleaning/ML models Plug models in without changing platform code; compare model versions Oversight body (HEA) Reviews national ETD output Aggregate counts and quality indicators

docs.title: 2.4 Operating environment
docs.text:
• Server portal (netd.ac.zm): Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS since November 2, 2026 (was 20.04.6; upgraded one LTS at a time, see docs/OPERATIONS.md), 2 vCPU, 3.8 GiB RAM, 2 GiB swap file, 162 GB free disk. It is shared with other live services: Apache (80/443), Tomcat (current portal, :8080), Orthanc, MySQL (8.4) and nginx, and the EMI Drupal site (Drupal 11 on PHP 8.5).
  • No Docker. Python 3.12 (standalone, via uv), Ruby 3.3 (ruby-build), OpenJDK 11, Solr 9.11 (slim), SQLite.
  • Browsers: current Chrome, Firefox, Edge and Safari, including mobile.

docs.title: 2.5 Design and implementation constraints
docs.text:
• C1 Must not disturb the live portal or other services on the server, and must not upgrade or remove system packages (apt was in a broken state on October 30, 2026). Exception (November 1, 2026): three leaf packages for OCR (FR-48) — tesseract-ocr, tesseract-ocr-eng, poppler-utils — were added after apt-get -s showed 7 new packages and nothing upgraded or removed.
  • C2 Memory budget: Solr heap ≤ 512 MB; web app ≤ 300 MB resident.
  • C3 Must not depend on actions by third parties (e.g. DNS changes). The /beta sub-path was used while both portals ran (October 30–31, 2026); retired in v0.8.
  • C4 Open-source components only; source code versioned on GitHub.
  • C5 ML models are Python; the cleaning tier must be Python.
  • C6 British English in the interface and documentation.

docs.title: 2.6 Assumptions and dependencies
docs.text:
• A1 HEI repositories expose OAI-PMH. Verified on October 30, 2026 for UNZA RIMS (https://rims.unza.ac.zm/server/oai/request) and UNILUS (https://research.unilus.ac.zm/server/oai/request). Both offer dim, etdms, oai_dc and others.
  • A2 Supervisor and department are not present in the harvested metadata of either sample source (0% completeness, measured on October 30, 2026). They will require text/PDF extraction or ML (FR-14).
  • A3 Full texts remain in the source IRs; NETD stores links only.

docs.title: 3. Specific requirements
docs.text: Priority: M = must (v0.1), S = should (v0.2), C = could (later).

docs.title: 3.1 External interface requirements
docs.text: ID Requirement Pri EI-1 The harvester shall act as an OAI-PMH 2.0 client supporting Identify, ListMetadataFormats, ListSets and ListRecords, with resumption tokens. M EI-2 The portal shall be served over HTTPS at the root of netd.ac.zm through the existing Apache server (reverse proxy), with HTTP redirected to HTTPS and the former /beta/ and old ETD Portal addresses (/portal, /summary, /harvester) redirected; the HTTPS proxy shall pass X-Forwarded-Proto: https so that form posts pass Rails' origin check. M EI-3 The portal shall offer a JSON view of search results and records (Blacklight .json). It follows the website's search interface and internal field names and may change; EI-6 is the stable interface. S EI-4 The system shall expose an OAI-PMH 2.0 data provider of canonical records at https://netd.ac.zm/oai, supporting all six verbs, the formats oai_dc and etdms (ETD-MS v1.1), one set per institution and per degree level (Masters, Doctoral, Postgraduate Diploma), resumption tokens, and incremental harvesting by the date a record last changed in the portal. M EI-5 The UI shall follow the style of Columbia's Academic Commons [R15]: system UI typography, a navy group bar, a serif wordmark with the search box, a link row (About, Explore), white pages with light cards, one blue for links and actions; facet sidebar and result list with badges on search pages. M EI-6 The system shall offer a read-only REST API at https://netd.ac.zm/api/v1 (FR-42 to FR-46), described by an OpenAPI 3 specification at /api/v1/openapi.yaml with an interactive reference on Developer Resources. It shall need no key, answer in JSON (UTF-8) with errors as {"error": {status, title, detail}} (400, 404, 429, 503), allow calls from other websites (CORS), and limit each address to 120 requests a minute per endpoint (export: 20 an hour). Field names within v1 shall not change; incompatible changes shall go into a new version, with the previous one kept for at least 6 months. M

docs.title: 3.2 Functional requirements
docs.text:
Source management and harvesting

ID Requirement Pri FR-1 Sources shall be configured in a registry file (harvester/sources.yml) giving id, name, short name, base URL, preferred metadata formats, ETD sets, and set-name rules. M FR-2 For each source, the harvester shall choose the first preferred format the source offers (default order dim, etdms, oai_dc). M FR-3 The harvester shall restrict harvesting to the configured ETD sets. M FR-4 The harvester shall support full and incremental (from= last successful run minus one day) harvests. M FR-5 The harvester shall record OAI deletions and remove deleted records from the index. M FR-6 The harvester shall retry on HTTP 500/502/503/504 and honour Retry-After. M FR-7 Each harvest run shall be logged (source, start/end, from-date, counts, status, message). M FR-8 The harvester shall store the set hierarchy (ListSets) for each source. M FR-9 Harvests shall run on a schedule (daily) without manual action. S FR-10 Fallback adapters shall be available for HEIs without working OAI-PMH: DSpace 7 REST API (v0.3, used for ZCAS); DSpace 6 XMLUI browse pages + per-item METS exports (v0.4, used for Mulungushi); CSV (v0.21): a file on the server or a published URL, in the template published on Developer Resources, with invalid rows reported and skipped and rows removed from the file deleted. S

Processing, cleaning and enrichment

ID Requirement Pri FR-11 Raw metadata shall be stored unmodified; processing shall be re-runnable from the raw store without re-harvesting. M FR-12 A crosswalk shall map dim, etdms and oai_dc to canonical fields: title, author, supervisor, subject, faculty, department, discipline, degree, degree level, year, abstract, URL, language, type, institution. M FR-13 Faculty/Department shall be derived from the set hierarchy where a source's collections represent units (per-source rule collections_are). M FR-14 Metadata filling. Fields the repository leaves empty (degree level, degree, discipline, supervisor, department, faculty) shall be filled by metadata-filling models working on the text of each ETD's front matter (FR-48), through a prediction cache (FR-49). Precedence per field: manual correction (FR-51) over harvested value over predicted value; a prediction fills a field only if the field is empty and the prediction's confidence is at least the display threshold (ml.show_threshold, 0.8), and it is marked as derived (FR-50). Free-text rules (v0.2) remain for harvested fields. (Deferred on October 31, 2026; resumed on November 1, 2026.) S FR-15 Every canonical field value shall carry provenance (harvested:, set:, text:, rule:, model:). M FR-16 Enrichers shall be pluggable as Python callables f(record) -> record, registered in enrichers.yml without code changes to the platform. M FR-17 Enrichers may set a confidence per field. Values below min_confidence shall stay searchable but shall not be used as facet values. M FR-18 Built-in rules shall normalise whitespace, ALL-CAPS titles (keeping the original), personal names, and ALL-CAPS unit names. M FR-19 Duplicate ETDs, in one source or across sources, shall be detected: by DOI, then by title (same or nearly the same, similarity ≥ 0.93 after folding case, accents and punctuation) with compatible authors (a shared name word, or a typing slip) and years at most 2 apart. A thesis deposited more than once shall be listed once in search results, facets and counts, under a main record (the admin's choice, or else the copy with a PDF and the most metadata); the other copies keep their record pages, which link to the main record, and stay available through OAI-PMH and the REST API (duplicate_of, other_copies; search returns main records only unless duplicates=include). Records are never merged or deleted. The admin panel lists the groups; an admin can mark a record as not a duplicate or choose a group's main record (stored as _duplicate corrections, kept across re-harvests) (Lighton, November 2, 2026). C

Discovery

ID Requirement Pri FR-20 Users shall search by keyword across all fields, or within Title, Author, Supervisor or Subject. M FR-21 Users shall filter by facets: Institution, Degree level, Faculty/School, Department, Programme/Discipline, Degree, Supervisor, Subject, Year (newest first; the 5 latest years visible, the rest behind "more »"). M FR-22 Users shall sort results from a "Sort by" menu beside the result count, as on Academic Commons [R15]: Best Match (default), Published Latest, Published Earliest, Title A-Z, Title Z-A. Results shall be shown 10 per page by default, as on Google Scholar, with a "Show" menu offering 20, 50 or 100 per page. M FR-23 Each search result shall show, as on Academic Commons [R15]: the title (link to the record); the authors; a line "YEAR · DEGREE · INSTITUTION" (degree name, or degree level when no name is recorded); an abstract snippet of up to three lines; the subjects as links to subject searches; and a Download PDF link when available. M FR-24 Record pages shall follow the Academic Commons record layout [R15]: year/type/degree-level kicker, title, authors, abstract; Subjects and Programme/Discipline as tag buttons linking to searches; a Files panel (name, type, size, download per file); all other metadata (institution, faculty, department, thesis advisors, degree, degree level, year, language, source record) in a "More About This Work" panel; and a top-right panel with Download, persistent link with copy, sharing links, rights and holding institution, a "Report a problem" button opening the form in FR-34, and an Analysis panel linking to the work on Google Scholar, where its "Cited by" count is shown. Google Scholar has no public API, so the count itself is not shown on the portal. M FR-25 Hierarchical browsing: a Browse by Faculty page (/browse, linked from the header) shall list each institution, its faculties or schools and, under each, its departments, with counts of theses (each thesis once, FR-19), each linking to the matching search. Faculty–department pairs are offered only where both values are facetable. S FR-26 Institution entry points (InvenioRDM "communities" equivalent): the home page lists each institution with its ETD count. Implemented in v0.2. S

Reporting

ID Requirement Pri FR-27 The administrator shall obtain a per-institution field-completeness report from the command line. M FR-28 A quality dashboard (completeness and ETD-MS compliance per HEI): public with overall figures only; the per-institution breakdown and suggested improvements in the admin panel until publication is agreed with HEA (Lighton, November 1, 2026). For each harvested institution (and overall) and element (the 12 ETD-MS 1.1 elements the portal uses, plus faculty, department and full-text PDF), it shall show the share of ETDs whose value is (a) supplied by the repository in the proper element, (b) present in the repository only in collection names or free text, (c) filled by the portal (models, corrections), or (d) missing; an ETD-MS compliance score at source (mean of (a) over the ETD-MS elements); completeness in the portal; suggested improvements per institution; and downloads as CSV and JSON. Recomputed after every scheduled run. C

Coverage and project information

ID Requirement Pri FR-29 An institution registry (harvester/institutions.yml) shall list every HEI with at least one HEA-accredited Master's or Doctoral programme [R12], [R13]. The home page and the Institution facet shall show every registry institution (the facet shows the top 10 rows, harvested institutions first, with a "more »" toggle for the rest), with 0 where nothing is harvested and the reason (no repository known, no ETD collection, no theses in the ETD collection yet, repository not reachable or not harvestable). M FR-30 The home page shall state that metadata is meant to be harvested from all institutions offering HEA-accredited Master's and PhD programmes, citing HEA. M FR-31 The portal (About page) and the repository (PUBLICATIONS.md) shall list the project details [R14], the project members with their roles as on the DataLab people page (the PI marked Principal Investigator), and the publications, dissertations and capstone reports based on the Zambia National ETD Portal project, with a short explanation of how they relate to the portal, from one source file (portal/config/publications.yml). M FR-35 Every page shall have a footer, as on Academic Commons [R15], with links to About, FAQ, Developer Resources and Credits, the contact address datalab@unza.zm, and a line crediting the DataLab Research Group (development) and ZAMREN (hosting). The About page shall credit both, with their logos. Developer Resources shall document the JSON (REST) API and the OAI-PMH interface (EI-4). Credits shall name DataLab and ZAMREN, the Core Team (Lighton Phiri, Lead Developer and Principal Investigator; Elijah Chileshe, Assistant Programmer/Analyst), and as Contributors and Former Team Members the students listed on the project page [R14]. M FR-34 Record pages shall offer a "Report a problem" popup form (problem type, message, name, email address, record URL). Each report shall be stored in the portal database and emailed to lighton.phiri@unza.ac.zm and datalab@unza.zm (subject (<portal name>) <problem>: <title>, reply-to the reporter) through an authenticated SMTP account; the form shall have a spam trap and a rate limit. M FR-36 Admin sign-in. The system shall provide an admin panel at /admin for the portal team only. Access shall require an email address and password; accounts shall be created, reset and disabled from the server's command line only (no self-registration). A new or reset account shall get a one-time password that must be changed at first sign-in (at least 12 characters). Sessions shall end after 2 hours of inactivity or 12 hours in total, and on sign-out. Each account shall have a role: "admin" (every admin page and action) or "viewer" (read-only, e.g. for HEA staff: the reports for HEA, metadata quality and usage pages, and changing its own password; every other admin page redirects to the reports and is left out of the menu). The role is set from the command line (November 2, 2026). M FR-37 Admin dashboard. The panel shall show every source with its loader, latest harvest (time, status, message), records in the staging store and in the search index, whether a harvest is running, and the number of open problem reports; a source page shall list its recent harvests. An administrator shall be able to start a harvest of one source ("Run now"); it shall never run at the same time as another harvest, including the nightly one. M FR-38 Problem reports in the panel. Reports received through FR-34 shall be listed (open or resolved), shown in full, and marked resolved or reopened with a note recording what was done; the panel shall record who resolved a report and when. M FR-39 CSV upload in the panel. An administrator shall be able to upload an institution's CSV file (FR-10, at most 50 MB); the system shall first show the result of the CSV check (rows, valid rows, each problem by line) and change nothing until the administrator confirms. On confirmation, the file shall replace the institution's current file (the previous one archived) and be loaded. A file with no valid rows shall not be loadable. M FR-40 Adding a CSV institution. While uploading, an administrator shall be able to choose an HEA-listed institution (FR-29) that has no source yet and give its short name; the system shall register it as a CSV source without editing the configuration files in the repository. S FR-41 Activity log. Every sign-in, failed sign-in attempt and change made through the panel (password changes, harvests started, CSV files checked and loaded, sources added, reports resolved or reopened), and account changes made from the command line, shall be recorded with the time, the account, the subject and the IP address, and shown in the panel. M FR-42 API search. GET /api/v1/records shall search records with keywords (all fields or one of title, author, supervisor, subject, using the portal's search weighting) and filters for institution, degree level (Masters, Doctoral or Postgraduate Diploma), year or year range, full text available, changed since a date, and exact faculty, department, discipline, degree, subject and supervisor; sort by relevance, newest, oldest, title or last change; page through at most 10,000 results, 1 to 100 per page (20 by default); and return the records with the total, page count and next/previous links. Unknown or invalid parameters shall be rejected with a message saying what is wrong. M FR-43 API record. GET /api/v1/records/{id} shall return one record: identifiers (portal id and OAI-PMH identifier), title, authors, supervisors, abstract, year, degree, degree level, discipline, faculty, department, subjects, language, type, rights, institution (id and name), links (portal page, source page, PDF, API) and files, which fields were derived by a model (FR-50; added in API 1.1.0), and when it last changed in the portal. M FR-44 API institutions. GET /api/v1/institutions shall list every HEA-listed institution (FR-29) with its id (when harvested), short name, postgraduate levels, record count, status, repository, harvest method and last harvest. M FR-45 API statistics. GET /api/v1/stats shall return the total, counts by institution, degree level (Masters, Doctoral, Postgraduate Diploma and unknown) and year, and for each institution and overall the percentage of records with supervisor, subject, faculty, department, degree, degree level, abstract and full text. S FR-46 Bulk export. GET /api/v1/export.csv and /api/v1/export.jsonl shall return every record (CSV with a header row and || between list values; JSON Lines with one API record per line), rebuilt at most every 6 hours. S FR-47 Postgraduate scope. The portal shall hold postgraduate work only: postgraduate diploma, master's and doctoral theses, dissertations and reports. When processing, a record whose degree level is identified (from the repository's degree level, or from its degree name, type or description text) as anything else shall be left out, as shall any record listed for exclusion for its source with a reason; records whose level cannot be identified shall be kept until it can be (FR-14). Raw harvested records shall be kept (FR-11), and every excluded record and its reason shall be listed (netd.cli report, admin source page). M FR-48 PDF text cache. For each record with a full-text link, the text of the first pages (8 per file) shall be extracted and cached, reading front-matter files first when a repository splits a thesis into several files (cover, preliminary pages, main document; at most 3 files). PDFs without a text layer (scans) shall be read with OCR (first 5 pages). A PDF shall be fetched again only when the record's files change, or on request after an error. Extraction shall run at low priority under the harvest lock, so it never overlaps a harvest. S FR-49 Prediction cache and models. Each model shall have a name and version and shall write, per record and field, its value(s), a confidence in 0..1, the evidence text it used, and a hash of its input; a model shall run again for a record only when that hash changes. Models shall see harvested values only, never other models' output. Predictions computed elsewhere (e.g. a Colab notebook) shall be loadable as JSON Lines into the same cache. The baseline model reads the title-page degree statement, the supervision statements (title page, approval page, acknowledgements) and the academic units named on the first pages. S FR-50 Derived values. A value filled by a model shall be marked "derived" on the record page (with the model and confidence, and a note that it may contain errors) and in the REST API record (derived object: field → method and confidence), without changing existing API fields (EI-6). Derived values shall be facetable when their confidence is at least min_confidence (FR-17). S FR-51 Manual corrections. A signed-in administrator shall be able to look up a record (by id or portal address), see each field's value and where it came from (harvested, rule, model with confidence, corrected), see all predictions with their evidence, and correct or clear any of degree level, degree, discipline, supervisor, department, faculty, subjects, year, title and authors. Corrections shall override harvested and predicted values, persist across re-harvests and reprocessing, be logged in the activity log (FR-40) with the administrator and an optional note, be removable, and take effect when the record's source is next processed (nightly, or on request with "Apply now"). S FR-52 Degree-level review. A predicted degree level below postgraduate with confidence at or above ml.level_auto_exclude (0.95) shall exclude the record under FR-47, the reason naming the model; between ml.level_review_min (0.6) and that threshold the record shall stay in the portal and be listed for review in the admin panel with the evidence and a PDF link. An administrator's decision (exclude, or keep as postgraduate) shall be stored as a correction, override the model and FR-47's level rule, and be logged. S FR-53 Evaluation. It shall be possible to draw a gold-standard sample stratified by institution for manual annotation (netd.cli gold-sample), and to report, per model, version and field, coverage, precision, recall and F1 against it at several confidence thresholds (netd.cli evaluate), so that each new model is compared with the baseline before it is enabled. S FR-54 Subject scheme. Besides each repository's own subject headings (inconsistent and often missing: 16.6% of records had none on November 1, 2026), every record shall carry standard fields of study from OpenAlex Topics (CC0): 4 domains, 26 fields and 252 subfields, identified by OpenAlex ids and URIs. The taxonomy version used shall be recorded with the model. M FR-55 Assignment. Fields of study shall be assigned to every record with a title or abstract by a model (FR-49 contract), at the most specific level the model is confident about: one subfield (two if the second is also likely), else the field, else the domain. They are derived values (FR-50), correctable in the admin panel (FR-51), and do not replace or alter harvested subjects. M FR-56 Exposure. The portal shall offer Research domain, Field of study and Subfield facets as its main subject facets and show the field of study (domain › field › subfield) on record pages with a link to OpenAlex; repository subjects shall be shown and searchable as "Keywords (from the repository)". The REST API shall add fields_of_study (id, URI, name, level, field, domain, confidence); OAI-PMH shall add <subject scheme="OpenAlex"> (etdms) and the name and URI as dc:subject (oai_dc). The FAQ and Developer Resources shall state the scheme, its source and version, how values are assigned, and that they can be corrected. M FR-60 Following new additions. The system shall record when each record first appears in the portal ("date added"; records present before November 1, 2026 take their institution's first harvest date), offer a "Newest Additions" sort, give Atom and RSS feeds of the newest additions for any search and filters (dated by date added) through a "Follow this search" page linked from results and the home page, and expose added_at and sort=added in the REST API (1.4.0). No accounts or personal data (phase 1); email alerts with confirmed subscriptions are deferred until after the handover to HEA (phase 2). S FR-58 Repository watch. The system shall check, weekly, every repository listed in the institution registry for institutions not yet harvested (repository page; OAI-PMH Identify; records listed overall and in the ETD sets named in the registry), keep the latest result, show it on the admin dashboard and in the weekly status email, and list changes since the previous check (a repository becoming reachable or unreachable, records appearing in its ETD sets). S FR-59 Guide for institutions. A public page shall explain to HEI librarians how to take part: the scope (postgraduate only), the repository route (reachable from outside the campus, OAI-PMH switched on, OAI index kept current, ETDs in their own collections, public PDFs, recommended fields) and the CSV route (template, required columns, published Google Sheet), linked from the home page, the footer, Developer Resources and the admin panel. S FR-61 Usage analytics without third-party trackers. The portal shall count, per day (UTC): home page visits, searches (first results page), Browse pages, record page views and PDF downloads (per record and institution, through the portal's own Download links, which redirect to the repository's file), and API and OAI-PMH requests (per endpoint or verb). Only the day, the kind of use, the record id and its institution are stored with each count: no IP address, browser details, cookie or search words. Requests from crawlers, link previews, prefetches and signed-in administrators are not counted (API and OAI-PMH requests are); crawlers are recognised by user agent, including scanners that send a browser-like user agent without a platform ("Mozilla/5.0 AppleWebKit/..."). Signed-in administrators see totals, a daily table, figures by institution, the most viewed records and most downloaded PDFs, and API and OAI-PMH use for the last 7, 30, 90 or 365 days, and can download the daily counts as CSV (/admin/usage). The FAQ says what is counted. Blacklight's search history (needed for "Back to search") is kept one day and is not written for crawlers; robots.txt keeps crawlers off facet combinations, feeds and data formats. Extension (November 2, 2026): the country and approximate city of each home visit, search, Browse page, record view and PDF download, looked up on the portal's server from an offline database and counted per day, the address discarded; the facet values chosen on first results pages that found records (never typed words); and, on each record page, its view and download counts, each with an icon (an eye for views, a download arrow for downloads; November 4, 2026). S FR-62 Department and faculty names. Within an institution, spellings of the same department shall be shown under one name in the record page, facets, Browse, the API and OAI-PMH: "&" read as "and", hyphen spacing and trailing fragments removed, values grouped by a key that ignores case, word order, plural endings and "of/and/the", each group shown under its most frequent spelling, and a value seen at most twice joined to a group with at least three times as many records whose key is nearly the same (similarity ≥ 0.92). The value as harvested or predicted is kept (department_orig_ssm); the staging store and the model predictions are not changed. Collections that are not faculties or schools may be mapped per source to a faculty and department, or to none (set_units in sources.yml). S FR-63 Reports for HEA. Signed-in administrators (and HEA staff once given administrator accounts) shall be able to produce, from /admin/etd-reports, reports as Excel workbooks (a Summary sheet with the filters, contents and notes, and one styled sheet per table with filters, a frozen header, data bars and a chart where useful) and as PDF (A4, title band, charts, tables with repeated headers, page numbers), or preview them in the browser: (a) per institution or for all institutions: summary and completeness, theses by year, degree level, year and degree level, type, faculty, faculty and department, and degree, and, for all institutions, every HEA institution with 0 where nothing is harvested; optionally usage (record views and PDF downloads by institution, most viewed records, readers by country; FR-61, with its caveats); (b) by supervisor: each supervisor name with theses by degree level and first and last year, and the theses under each supervisor with whether the supervisor came from the repository or the portal; (c) custom: filters (institution, years, degree level, type, faculty, department, field of study, supervisor name, words in title or abstract), grouping by one field or a table of two fields, and a list of theses with chosen columns (including which values the portal filled). Counts are of distinct theses (other copies left out, FR-19). Each report run is written to the activity log. Reports are not public (Lighton, November 2, 2026). S FR-64 Supervisor names. Within an institution, spellings of the same supervisor shall be shown under one name in the record page, facets, Browse, the reports for HEA, the API and OAI-PMH ("J. Phiri", "Jackson Phiri", "Dr Phiri J"). Two spellings are the same person when the surnames are equal and the given names or initials, read in order, agree (initials equal; full names equal or one a prefix of the other; the same full names in another order also agree). For common surnames a spelling joins a group only when it agrees with every spelling in it and exactly one group qualifies, or exactly one shares a department (failing that, a faculty) with the spelling's records; a bare surname is never joined. Each group is shown under its fullest spelling in ordinary capitals. The values as harvested or predicted are kept (supervisor_orig_ssm), shown on the record page ("As written in the record") and still found by a supervisor search; the staging store and the model predictions are not changed. S FR-65 How to cite. Each record page shall show, in its side panel, a citation of the thesis in APA style, with a choice of the citation styles OJS offers (ACM, ACS, APA, ABNT, Chicago, Harvard, IEEE, MLA, Turabian, Vancouver), a Copy button, and downloads for reference managers (RIS for EndNote, Zotero and Mendeley; BibTeX). Citations are produced from the official Citation Style Language styles with British English terms, as an item of type thesis (authors, year, title (put into sentence case when the repository wrote it in capitals, keeping place names and acronyms such as Zambia and HIV), "Doctoral thesis", "Master's thesis" or "Postgraduate diploma dissertation" from the degree level, the awarding institution). The link cited is the item on the institution's own repository, which holds the version of record; the portal's record page is cited only when the repository link is unusable. Repository links are built from the OAI identifier on the repository's current host (https://<host>/handle/<handle>), not taken from dc.identifier.uri, which names old or local hosts for many records (all UNZA records named dspace.unza.zm, which is no longer in DNS; November 4, 2026); a source can keep its harvested links (record_url: harvested). Citation requests are not counted as usage and are kept out of search engines. (Lighton, November 4, 2026.) S FR-66 Discoverability. Each record page shall carry the bibliographic meta tags Google Scholar reads (Highwire Press: citation_title, citation_author, citation_publication_date, citation_dissertation_institution, citation_dissertation_name, citation_publisher, citation_abstract, citation_abstract_html_url, citation_pdf_url pointing to the repository's PDF, citation_keywords, citation_language), a description and Open Graph tags for link previews, and a canonical link to itself. The portal shall publish /sitemap.xml listing the home page, Browse and every listed record page (other copies of duplicates left out), named in robots.txt. (Lighton, November 4, 2026; Google Scholar showed no portal records.) S FR-67 Similar theses. Each record page shall list up to five similar theses held in the portal (Solr MoreLikeThis on title, abstract and keywords; other copies of duplicates left out), each with its year and institution, in a section the reader can collapse and expand, closed by default and marked "+" (closed) or "−" (open) on the right, as PubMed Central's Resources sections (Lighton, November 5, 2026). (Lighton, November 4, 2026.) S FR-68 Record page addresses. Each record page shall be at https://netd.ac.zm/theses/<short id>, where the short id is the record id without the DSpace default handle prefix 123456789 (/theses/zcas-298 for record zcas-123456789-298); ids without that prefix are used unchanged, and no short id may stand for two records. The PDF and citation addresses follow (/theses/<short id>/pdf, /theses/<short id>/cite). Every earlier address (/catalog/<record id>, its /pdf and /cite variants and .json) and /theses/<record id> shall redirect permanently (HTTP 301) to the new one, keeping the query string. The sitemap, canonical link, Google Scholar and Open Graph tags, citations, feeds, the OAI-PMH record link and the API's links.portal use the new address. Record ids in the index, the store, usage counts, OAI-PMH identifiers and the API are unchanged; the API also accepts the short id. Search stays at /catalog. (Lighton, November 4, 2026, before search engines index the old addresses.) S FR-69 Cited by. Each thesis shall be matched, about weekly, to a work in OpenAlex by normalised title (word overlap of at least 0.8) and year (within one year); only a dissertation (or an untyped item without a DOI) may match, never a journal article, even one derived from the thesis or merged with it in OpenAlex; a work matching two theses matches neither. When the matched work is cited, the record page shall show "Cited by N" with the citing works (title, year, link to the DOI or OpenAlex) in a section the reader can collapse, and credit OpenAlex; nothing is shown when N is 0. The job shall stay within OpenAlex's free daily allowance and never stop the nightly harvest. Search pages shall offer a "Cited" filter and a "Most Cited" sort, and result cards shall show "Cited by N" when N is above 0. The REST API record shall carry the OpenAlex work id and the citing works (count null when the thesis is not matched), with a cited filter and a cited sort (API 1.7.0); OAI-PMH records shall carry the OpenAlex work address as an identifier; the HEA reports (FR-63) shall count matched and cited theses, list cited theses by institution and the most cited theses, and offer a "Cited by" column and a cited-only filter. Citations between theses from their own reference lists are out of scope (backlog). (Lighton, November 4, 2026.) When OpenAlex asks the job to retry later (busy), the job shall wait as asked, up to five minutes a run, and log the run as rate-limited rather than as the daily budget; an API key that OpenAlex rejects shall not stop the job, which then continues without a key and logs a warning (Lighton, November 5, 2026, after the first nightly run was refused). S FR-71 Filter list addresses. The full list of values of one search filter (the list behind a filter's "more" link, shown in a pop-up or on its own page) shall be at https://netd.ac.zm/theses/filters/<name>, with a readable name per filter (institution, full-text, degree-level, research-domain, field-of-study, subfield, faculty, department, programme, degree, supervisor, keywords, year, author), the search kept in the query string; sorting and paging links inside the list use the same address. Blacklight's /catalog/facet/<field> addresses shall redirect permanently (HTTP 301) to the new ones, keeping the query string and format. A filter made of fixed queries ("Citations (OpenAlex)") has no list and answers 404. Searches stay on the home page (/?q=). (Lighton, November 5, 2026: the HEA presentation slides linked to /catalog/facet/…, the only /catalog/ address readers could still reach.) S FR-57 Model and evaluation. The field-of-study model shall run on the server's CPU (no GPU), be trained on OpenAlex works labelled by OpenAlex (reproducibly, from scripts in the repository), and be evaluated on held-out OpenAlex works and on an annotated sample of portal records before each new version is enabled; results are recorded in docs/PAPER-PLAN.md. S FR-33 The landing page shall show a one-line introduction, two prominent buttons — Explore Master's Manuscripts and Explore PhD Manuscripts (degree-level filtered searches) — "stats at a glance" (total ETDs, master's, doctoral, with full-text PDF, institutions contributing of those listed, years covered) and the contributing institutions, with the not-yet-harvested HEA institutions behind a toggle. M FR-32 For every ETD whose repository exposes it, the portal shall link directly to the full-text file (bitstream), preferring the largest PDF, on result cards and record pages, and offer a Full text facet (PDF available / other file / metadata only). Files stay in the source repositories. M

docs.title: 3.3 Non-functional requirements
docs.text: ID Category Requirement Pri NFR-1 Performance Search result pages shall render in ≤ 1.5 s (server time, p95) for 10,000 records. M NFR-2 Capacity v0.1 shall handle ≥ 50,000 records within constraint C2. M NFR-3 Resource Total added resident memory ≤ 1 GB under normal load. M NFR-4 Availability Services shall restart automatically (systemd) after failure or reboot. M NFR-5 Isolation Services run as unprivileged user netd; Solr binds to 127.0.0.1 only. M NFR-6 Maintainability Adding a new DSpace source shall need only a registry entry. M NFR-7 Portability Installation scripted (deploy/install-server.sh, deploy/deploy.sh). M NFR-8 Usability Responsive layout; WCAG 2.1 AA colour contrast for badges and links. S NFR-9 Security HTTPS for netd.ac.zm with a valid certificate (in place since October 30, 2026; Let's Encrypt, auto-renewing). S NFR-10 Politeness At most one concurrent request per source. M NFR-11 Recoverability The staging store and portal database shall be backed up nightly, verified by checksum, kept 14 days on the server and about 60 days off the server (Google Drive); a restore procedure shall be documented and tested. M NFR-12 Monitoring The maintainer shall be emailed when a scheduled job or service fails, when a source's latest harvest failed or is more than 30 hours old, when the index disagrees with the store, and when the public site stops serving results (once per outage, plus recovery); a weekly status email shall confirm the alert path works. M NFR-14 Concurrency The staging store shall allow reading (admin panel, reports, backups) while a harvest, text extraction or correction writes to it (SQLite WAL mode, 120 s busy timeout); only the netd user shall open it for writing. M NFR-13 Admin security The admin panel shall be served over HTTPS only, with passwords stored as bcrypt hashes, a signed HTTP-only session cookie, CSRF protection on every form, at most 10 sign-in attempts per 3 minutes from one address, no caching of admin pages, and admin pages excluded from search engines. M NFR-15 Configurability Everything that identifies an installation (country name and adjective, time zone, portal name, wordmark and host, regulator, public contact, problem-report recipients, mail senders, credits) shall be read from one file, config/country.yml (path overridable with NETD_COUNTRY), by the portal, the harvester and the deployment scripts; a missing file, a missing required key or an unknown time zone shall stop start-up with a message naming the file and the key. The Zambian file shall reproduce the Zambian pages and API responses unchanged. Other countries copy an example from config/examples/. The interface text of the pages shall be kept in locale files (portal/config/locales/en.yml, keys under netd.), with the configuration's names interpolated, so that a translation or a change of wording is one file per language (packaging P4, in parts). (Lighton, November 4, 2026: open-source release for other countries; docs/PACKAGING-PLAN.md.) S

docs.title: 3.4 Data requirements
docs.text: The canonical record is a JSON object stored in SQLite (records.data): id, source, institution, institution_short, oai_id, datestamp, title[], author[], supervisor[], subject[], faculty[], department[], degree[], degree_level[], year[], abstract[], url[], language[], type[], provenance{field: origin}, confidence{field: 0..1}, derived{field: {method, confidence}}, facetable{field: bool}, raw_fields[]. Provenance values: harvested:<element>, set:<setSpec>, rule:<name>, model:<name>-<version>, corrected:<administrator e-mail>. Metadata-filling tables in the same store: pdf_text (record, files read, status ok/ocr/no_text/ocr_failed/too_large/error, pages, text, text hash), predictions (record, field, model, version, value, confidence, input hash, evidence), corrections (record, field or _scope, value, note, administrator, time) and level_review (record, predicted level, confidence, model, evidence, status).

Met FR-49 Test: predict twice (second run recomputes nothing); model versions 1–7 refined on real text with random-sample checks of values and evidence November 1, 2026: titlepage-rules v7 over 3,905 texts; values at confidence ≥ 0.8: degree level 3,622, degree 3,607, discipline 2,996, supervisor 2,054, faculty 501, department 277. Postgraduate scope (FR-47). After the crosswalk and the enrichers, cli.exclusion() decides whether a record enters records: it is left out if its source lists its oai_id under exclude_records (with a reason), or if its degree_level is identified and not in scope.degree_levels (default Doctoral, Masters, Postgraduate Diploma). Records of unknown level are kept. Excluded records go to excluded with the reason (rebuilt for a source on every processing run) and are shown by netd.cli report and on the admin source page; raw_records is untouched, so an exclusion is undone by removing it from sources.yml. Indexing then deletes from Solr every document of the source that records no longer holds (index.ids()), which also covers records deleted at the source. Levels come from the repository's own value, normalised, or from DEGREE_PAT over the degree name, type, description and collection names, postgraduate levels first; the ML models (FR-14) will fill the unknown levels later through the same field.

  • Text cache (textcache.py, FR-48). front_urls() orders a record's PDFs so files named cover/title come first, then other front-matter names (prelim, abstract, declaration, approval, certificate), then the rest; with no front-matter file only the first PDF is read; at most 3. extract-text downloads each file (≤ 60 MB, 2 threads fetching, SQLite written from the main thread only), keeps the first 8 pages with pypdf, and stores status ok, no_text (no text layer), too_large or error. ocr-text takes the no_text rows one at a time: pdftoppm at 200 dpi, greyscale, first 5 pages, then tesseract (English), both under nice 19; status ocr or ocr_failed. The url column holds the files read, so a change in the record's files makes it pending again. Both commands run under run.lock in batches (500 PDFs, 50 OCRs), so a nightly harvest waits at most one batch.
  • Prediction cache (cache.py, FR-49). predictions is keyed by (record, field, model) and holds version, value list, confidence, input hash and evidence. predict.run() builds each record's input from its PDF text and the harvested values of the fields the model USES (values with provenance model: or corrected: are removed, so models never learn from each other), hashes it with the model version, and calls predict() only when the hash changed; fields a model covers but finds nothing for are stored as [], so they are not recomputed. prepare(texts) gives a model corpus-level state (the baseline's word counts). load-predictions accepts JSON Lines from other environments.
  • Overlay (overlay.py, FR-14, FR-50 to FR-52), called by do_process after the enrichers and before cli.exclusion(). A record with neither predictions nor corrections is returned untouched (byte-identical, so OAI-PMH datestamps do not move). Otherwise, for each predicted field that is empty and not corrected, the best prediction is applied if its confidence ≥ ml.show_threshold; it sets the value, provenance[field] = model:<name>-<version>, confidence[field] and derived[field]. A predicted level below postgraduate is applied only at ≥ ml.level_auto_exclude (FR-47 then excludes the record, naming the model); between ml.level_review_min and that it goes to level_review instead. Corrections then overwrite (or clear) fields with provenance = corrected:<e-mail>. A _scope correction is returned to cli.exclusion(), where include keeps the record whatever FR-47's level rule says and exclude removes it with the administrator's note. save_review() rebuilds the pending rows for the processed sources; decided rows stay.
  • Baseline model titlepage-rules (models/titlepage.py). Degree statement: a statement keyword (fulfilment, requirement, submitted, award) followed within 200 characters by a degree head (Master/Doctor/Bachelor/Postgraduate Diploma of/in), parsed into degree, discipline and level (0.96); otherwise a degree name on the first three pages (0.82); otherwise an abbreviation such as MSc or PhD (0.70, level only). Supervisors (v10, v11 additions: title words never name parts, bare initials in a row, title + surname alone when the name ends there, up to eight words in "for his … supervision", "and [academic] mentor" / "and co-supervisor", "X (Supervisor)" at 0.80): labelled lines "Supervisor:" (0.92), "Supervisor Dr X" without a colon (0.90), "supervised by" (0.90), "under the supervision of" (0.88), acknowledgements "my [up to two words] supervisor(s)[ and mentor][,;:][ namely] Dr X, Prof Y and Dr Z" (up to four people, 0.86) and "Dr X , my supervisor" (0.82), "Dr X for his/her [able] supervision", "for accepting to supervise", "who supervised" (0.80), "X (principal/co-supervisor)" (0.75); name parts may be bare initials ("W Chakanika", "W.W"); names are cut at words that are not names (Sign, Dissertation, Public Health, MMed …), lose titles (including "Dr ." and "D r."), and all-caps names are title-cased. Patterns that start with a name are tried only within 120 characters before an occurrence of "supervis" (unbounded, they backtracked for up to 29 s on one OCRed page of acronyms). Supervisor text is rejoined without one-letter fragments (_rejoin(names=True)), and apostrophes inside surnames are closed up ("Hang ’ombe"). Units: "Department of …" → department, "School of …"/"Faculty of …" → faculty, from the first three pages (0.88 on page one, else 0.78). Text extraction often splits words ("M aster", "Eco nomics"); degree keywords are matched letter by letter with optional spaces, and other words are rejoined when the joined word is more frequent in the corpus than the rarer fragment.
  • Evaluation (evaluate.py, FR-53). gold-sample writes a CSV stratified by institution (proportional, at least 20 each) with harvested values and empty gold_* columns; evaluate normalises values (case, accents, titles, unit words; people by surname with compatible initials, one-to-one, apostrophes ignored, since v0.29; before, surname and first initial) and prints coverage, precision, recall and F1 per model, version and field at thresholds 0, 0.8 and 0.95. Corrections are a second source of labels.
  • Fields of study (FR-54 to FR-57). Model openalex-fos (models/fieldofstudy.py): title + abstract (harvested only) → sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 sentence embedding via fastembed (ONNX, CPU, about 90 MB on disk under harvester/models/fastembed) → multinomial logistic regression over the 252 OpenAlex subfields (weights models/data/openalex-fos-v1.npz, 252 × 384; taxonomy models/data/openalex-taxonomy.json). decide() backs off: subfield if p ≥ 0.30 (a second if p ≥ 0.30), else the field whose subfields sum to ≥ 0.40 (version 2; tuned on held-out works, see the report), else the most likely domain, so every record with text gets a value. Values are OpenAlex ids in the canonical field field_of_study; the overlay applies them with the per-field threshold ml.thresholds.field_of_study: 0.0. Models exposing predict_batch() are called in chunks of 256. index.fos_docs() turns ids into fos_domain_ssim, fos_field_ssim, fos_subfield_ssim (facets), fos_tsim (searched with the default and subject qf) and fos_ssm (JSON per value for the record page, API and OAI-PMH). Training data: tools/openalex_training.py (taxonomy and about 120 English works with abstracts per subfield, labelled by OpenAlex's primary topic) and tools/train_fieldofstudy.py (85/15 stratified split; report in models/data/openalex-fos-v1-report.md).
  • Walkthrough: notebooks/netd26-03-ml_metadata_filling-walkthrough.ipynb documents and runs each step above on a sample of public records, in a throwaway store, with the earlier DataLab work it builds on.
  • Configuration (enrichers.yml, key ml): show_threshold 0.8, level_auto_exclude 0.95, level_review_min 0.6; nightly (true), nightly_pdfs (300 per source) and nightly_ocr (30).

  • Nightly (cli.nightly_ml): the scheduled run extracts text for new or changed records, OCRs a few scans and runs predict after harvesting and before processing, so new ETDs get derived values the same night. Errors there are printed and skipped; the harvest, processing and indexing go on.

  • Usage counts (portal database storage/production.sqlite3, FR-61). usage_counts(day date, event, record_id, institution, hits), unique on (day, event, record_id, institution); event is one of home, search, browse, record_view, pdf_download, api (record_id = endpoint), oai (record_id = verb). Days are UTC. Nothing identifying a visitor is stored; rows are kept indefinitely (aggregate data). Backed up with the portal database. Places and facet values (since November 2, 2026): usage_places and usage_facets, as above; the reader's address is looked up in memory (request.remote_ip, set from Apache's X-Forwarded-For) and discarded. Attribution "IP Geolocation by DB-IP" (CC BY 4.0) on /admin/usage and the FAQ.

docs.text:
OaiController (portal/app/controllers/oai_controller.rb) answers OAI-PMH 2.0 at https://netd.ac.zm/oai. It reads Solr only, so the harvester's SQLite store is never touched by web requests, and it needs no new service.

Aspect Design Verbs Identify, ListMetadataFormats, ListSets, ListIdentifiers, ListRecords, GetRecord; GET or POST; repeated, missing or illegal arguments give badArgument, an unknown verb gives badVerb Identifiers oai:netd.ac.zm:<Solr id>, e.g. oai:netd.ac.zm:unza-123456789-9150 Datestamp updated_dtsi: when the record's canonical content last changed (records.updated_at, which Store.put_record leaves alone when a reprocessed record is unchanged). Granularity YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ; from/until accept days or seconds (same granularity for both) Sets inst:<source id> (from a Solr pivot of source_ssi and institution_ssim) and level:masters, level:doctoral (degree_level_ssim) Formats oai_dc; etdms (ETD-MS v1.1, elements in schema order, supervisors as contributor role="advisor", degree with name, level, discipline (or department) and grantor). Identifiers are the portal record page, the source landing page and the full-text link Paging 100 records per page; Solr cursorMark with sort=id asc. Resumption tokens are stateless: URL-safe Base64 JSON of prefix, set, date bounds, cursor mark, cursor and a 24-hour expiry; completeListSize and cursor are given Deletions deletedRecord=transient: records the harvester removes disappear from Solr Errors badVerb, badArgument, cannotDisseminateFormat, idDoesNotExist, noRecordsMatch (also for an unknown set), badResumptionToken; noSetHierarchy does not apply Monitoring netd.cli check fails if Identify does not answer (NFR-12) Verification tests/oai_conformance.py (Sickle and lxml): validates responses against the OAI-PMH and oai_dc schemas, checks ETD-MS element order, harvests every record in each format through resumption tokens, and exercises sets, dates, GetRecord and every error condition

docs.title: 5.2 Admin panel (FR-36 to FR-41)
docs.text:
The panel is part of the Rails portal (no new service). Every admin controller inherits from Admin::BaseController, which includes AdminAuthentication; public controllers never do. Accounts have a role (users.role): admin, or viewer (read-only, for HEA staff). Admin::BaseController#require_role lets a viewer reach only the controllers in VIEWER_PAGES (etd_reports, quality, usage, passwords, sessions) and redirects every other admin request (any verb) to the reports; the admin bar shows a viewer only those pages. Roles are set with deploy/ops/netd-user.sh add ... ROLE=viewer or netd-user.sh role EMAIL=... ROLE=... (which also signs the account out).

Page Route Controller Requirement Sign in / out GET/POST /admin/sign-in, DELETE /admin/sign-out Admin::SessionsController (rate-limited) FR-36 Change password /admin/password/edit Admin::PasswordsController (forced while must_change_password) FR-36 Dashboard /admin Admin::DashboardController#index FR-37 Source page, Run now /admin/sources/<id>, POST /admin/sources/<id>/run Admin::DashboardController#source, #run FR-37 Problem reports /admin/reports, /admin/reports/<id> Admin::ProblemReportsController FR-38 Upload CSV (check, then load) /admin/csv/new, POST /admin/csv, POST /admin/csv/load Admin::CsvUploadsController FR-39, FR-40 Activity log /admin/log Admin::EventsController FR-41 Correct a record (lookup box in the admin bar; record page with values, provenance, corrections and predictions; Apply now) GET /admin/records?id=, /admin/records/<id>, POST /admin/records/<id>/corrections, DELETE /admin/records/<id>/corrections/<field>, POST /admin/records/<id>/apply Admin::RecordsController FR-51 Degree-level review (waiting / decided) /admin/review, POST /admin/review/<id> (decision=exclude\|include) Admin::ReviewsController FR-52 Duplicates (groups, decisions) /admin/duplicates, POST /admin/duplicates/<id> (decision=distinct\|primary); decisions removed through the record's corrections Admin::DuplicatesController FR-19 Usage (totals, by day, by institution, most viewed and downloaded, API and OAI-PMH; 7/30/90/365 days; CSV) /admin/usage, /admin/usage.csv?days=n Admin::UsageController FR-61 ETD reports for HEA (per institution, by supervisor, custom; preview, Excel, PDF) /admin/etd-reports, /admin/etd-reports/:kind, .xlsx, .pdf Admin::EtdReportsController, HeaReport, ReportXlsx, ReportPdf FR-63

Corrections and review decisions are written by netd.cli correct / uncorrect (the panel opens the staging store read-only, as for CSV loading) and logged as record_corrected, correction_removed, level_review_excluded, level_review_kept, duplicate_rejected, duplicate_primary_chosen and reprocess_started. A duplicate decision starts reprocess for the record's source at once. "Apply now" runs netd.cli reprocess --source <id> (process and index, no harvest) under the harvest lock; when the lock is held, the change waits for the next run.

Sign-in and session (FR-36, NFR-13): SessionsController#create checks the bcrypt hash, creates a sessions row and sets the signed, HTTP-only, Secure, SameSite=Lax cookie netd_admin_session holding its id. Each request looks the session up, rejects it if the account is disabled or the session has been idle for 2 hours or is 12 hours old, and refreshes its updated_at at most once a minute. A one-time password (from netd-user.sh add or reset) sends the user to the password page until it is changed; changing it signs out the account's other sessions. Admin responses carry Cache-Control: no-store and X-Robots-Tag: noindex, and robots.txt disallows /admin.

The panel and the harvester (FR-37, FR-39, FR-40): the portal reads the staging store read-only and never writes to it. Anything that changes data runs netd.cli as a background process, as the same netd user, under flock on harvester/run.lock; the nightly netd-harvest.service takes the same lock (waiting up to 2 hours), so harvests never overlap. docs.title: 5.3 REST API v1 (EI-6, FR-42 to FR-46)
docs.text:
Since API 1.1.0 each record carries derived (FR-50), built by ApiRecord.derived from the Solr field derived_ssm (one JSON object per derived field: field, method, confidence); field names follow the API (supervisors, subjects). The addition changes no existing field (EI-6).

A read-only JSON API inside the Rails portal. Its controllers inherit from Api::V1::BaseController (ActionController::API: no sessions, cookies or CSRF), which adds CORS headers, the per-address rate limit and JSON error handling. Like the OAI-PMH provider, it reads Solr only. The contract is portal/app/views/static_files/openapi.text.erb, served at /api/v1/openapi.yaml (OpenAPI 3.0.3), which Developer Resources renders with Swagger UI at /developers/api.

Endpoint Controller Solr use Requirement GET /api/v1/records RecordsController#index /select: q with edismax and the portal's qf/pf (per field through ${title_qf} etc.), filters as fq ({!term}, {!terms}, ranges), start/rows FR-42 GET /api/v1/records/{id} RecordsController#show {!term f=id} FR-43 GET /api/v1/institutions InstitutionsController#index facet on institution_ssim; joined with InstitutionRegistry and Harvester (source ids, last runs) FR-44 GET /api/v1/stats StatsController#index facets on source_ssi, degree_level_ssim, year_isi, and source_ssi once per completeness field with an fq for its presence (9 requests, cached 10 minutes) FR-45 GET /api/v1/export.csv, .jsonl ExportsController#show cursorMark over all records, 500 at a time, sort=id asc FR-46 
flowchart LR
  C[API client or browser] -->|GET /api/v1/...| AP[Apache TLS]
  AP --> B[Api::V1::BaseController<br/>CORS, rate limit, errors]
  B --> R[RecordsController]
  B --> I[InstitutionsController]
  B --> S[StatsController]
  B --> E[ExportsController]
  R --> AR[ApiRecord<br/>stable field names]
  E --> AR
  R --> SO[(Solr core netd)]
  I --> SO
  S --> SO
  E --> SO
  I --> REG[InstitutionRegistry<br/>institutions.yml]
  I --> H[Harvester<br/>sources, last runs]
  S --> CA[(Rails cache<br/>10 min)]
  I --> CA
  E --> F[(tmp/api_export<br/>records.csv / .jsonl)]
  • Representation. ApiRecord maps Solr documents to the public field names (title, authors, supervisors, degree_level, institution {id, name}, links {portal, source, pdf, api}, files, updated_at), so index changes do not reach clients. Lists are always arrays and missing single values are null.
  • Paging. page/per_page up to 10,000 results (Solr start/rows stay cheap at that depth); the response gives meta.total, meta.pages and links.next/prev. Complete copies come from the export or OAI-PMH, which page with cursorMark.
  • Export. Built on demand into portal/tmp/api_export/ when the file is missing or more than 6 hours old, under an exclusive lock so concurrent requests wait for one build; written to a temporary file and renamed, then sent with Last-Modified.
  • Limits and errors. Rails 8 rate_limit (cache-store counters, per address and controller): 120 a minute, and 20 an hour for the export. Unknown parameters, bad values and paging beyond the limit give 400 with a specific message; unknown paths 404; Solr unavailable 503.
  • Versioning. The version is in the path. Within v1 fields are only added, never renamed or removed; an incompatible change means /api/v2, with v1 kept for at least 6 months (EI-6). The older /catalog.json view (EI-3) is unchanged and documented as subject to change.

  • All NETD services run as the unprivileged user netd (NFR-5) and are installed under /opt/netd.
  • Admin panel state on the server: accounts, sessions and the activity log in the portal database; CSV files in harvester/uploads/<id>/ (current records.csv, earlier ones in archive/); panel-added sources in harvester/sources.local.yml. The nightly backup includes all three (csv-sources.tgz holds the files). A harvest started from the panel runs inside the Puma service's process group, so restarting the portal (for example during a deployment) stops it; the next run finishes the job.
  • No Docker (C1). Python comes via uv; Ruby is compiled with ruby-build (rebuilt in place after an OS release upgrade: deploy/ops/upgrade/rebuild-ruby.sh). System packages are not upgraded or removed; the only additions are tesseract-ocr, tesseract-ocr-eng and poppler-utils for OCR (FR-48, November 1, 2026).
  • The staging store is in WAL mode with a 120 s busy timeout (NFR-14). Only netd opens it (the backup runs sqlite3 .backup as netd through runuser), so no root-owned -wal/-shm files can block the harvester.
  • PDF text extraction and OCR run as transient units (systemd-run --unit=netd-mltext --uid=netd --nice=10) or by hand, in batches under run.lock; see docs/OPERATIONS.md.
  • Apache sites for netd.ac.zm live in deploy/apache/ and are installed by deploy.sh, which backs up the previous files in /opt/netd/. Rollback: restore those backups and restart Apache.
  • Operations (NFR-11, NFR-12): every NETD unit has OnFailure=netd-alert@%n.service, which emails the unit's status and log. The harvest service ends with netd.cli check, which fails if a source's latest run failed or is stale, or if Solr per-source counts fall below 90% of the store. netd-backup.sh writes a dated folder only when every step succeeds, and netd-backup-to-gdrive.sh copies and verifies it with rclone (own OAuth client, scope drive.file, since November 3, 2026; a second destination is one more remote in the script's REMOTES, which is how HEA's own storage is added at the handover). The Solr index is not backed up because it is rebuilt from the store. Details and the restore procedure are in docs/OPERATIONS.md.
  • The earlier ETD Portal (Tomcat :8080) is no longer proxied; Tomcat keeps running because it hosts other applications.

docs.title: 8.1 Country configuration (NFR-15)
docs.text:
• config/country.yml (repository root; /opt/netd/config/country.yml on the server) holds the installation's identity: country (name, adjective, IANA time_zone), portal (name, wordmark, host), regulator, contact (public email, reports_to), mail (from, sender), credits, locale. config/examples/zambia/ is the shipped example. NETD_COUNTRY names another file.
  • Portal: portal/config/netd_country.rb defines Netd (plain Ruby, YAML and TZInfo only) and is required from config/application.rb after Bundler.require, so production.rb (mailer host) and every class can use it. Netd.config loads and validates once (required keys, time zone) and freezes the hash; accessors host, base_url, portal_name, contact_email, reports_to, mail_from, mail_sender, time_zone, time_zone_label ("Lusaka"), country_name, country_adjective, wordmark (two parts, checked at load), regulator_name, regulator_short_name, regulator_url, regulator_register_url, credits (each entry needs name, url, role; checked at load), credit(role), credit_title, credit_alt and keep_capitals. Read by OaiController (base URL, repository identifier, admin e-mail, record links), ApiRecord, the API's 404 text, ApplicationMailer, ProblemMailer, AdminHelper#admin_time, the quality pages, the dashboard, ReportPdf, ReportXlsx, the footer and the For Institutions, FAQ and Developer Resources pages. Rails' own config.time_zone stays UTC (stored and API times are UTC).
  • Harvester: netd/config.py (load, get, host, base_url, portal_name), used for user agents (repocheck, csvload, textcache, citedby) and the gold-sample links of ml.evaluate (no effect on scores). python -m netd.config --env prints the deployment settings.
  • Deployment: deploy.sh writes /opt/netd/deploy/site.env (NETD_HOST, NETD_BASE_URL, NETD_PORTAL_NAME, NETD_CONTACT_EMAIL, NETD_TIME_ZONE; not in git) right after the harvester environment; an invalid file stops the deployment there. netd-probe.sh sources it; netd-alert.py reads it and still sends alerts without it. The release archive (access/release.sh) includes config/.
  • Page text (P3b): the header component (group bar link and wordmark), footer (developer logo, description sentence built from credits in order, "developed by the …" using article), home text, About and Credits (logos looped from credits with class, logo_height, title and alternative text), FAQ, For Institutions, Developer Resources, page titles, admin CSV upload and reports pages, the problem-report e-mail body, OAI-PMH repositoryName, the RIS DB field, the /api/v1/institutions source note, the institution report note and the harvester's "not in the … institution list" error. Blacklight's application_name is set in config/locales/netd_country.rb (a Ruby locale file read after the gem's locales), replacing blacklight.en.yml. Citation::KEEP merges KEEP_GENERAL (continents, directions, diseases, international bodies, Roman numerals) with citation.keep_capitals. The templates keep the exact markup (attribute order, white space) so that Zambian pages are byte-identical; publications.yml still supplies the project, members and publications (its credits.hosting block is no longer read).
  • Interface text (P4, from P4a): portal/config/locales/en.yml holds the pages' wording under netd.<area>.<key> (P4a: header, footer, home; P4b: common, about, credits, faq, contribute, developers, api_docs; P4c: browse, follow, quality, follow_search; P4d: record (with record.about for the More About This Work rows and record.report for the problem-report form), results, facets). Text inside the record page's inline script is written with j nt(...) (escape_javascript), so that a translation with an apostrophe cannot break the script. P4e: the labels of facets, record fields, search fields and sort options are no longer label: values in CatalogController but keys under blacklight.search.fields.<context>.<field> (context facet, show, search or sort), which Blacklight 9 reads first; the two places that read a facet's label (FollowController, the admin usage page) call display_label('facet'), and the Citations facet's one item takes its label from the helper cited_facet_label (netd.facets.cited). The fixed code lists InstitutionRegistry::STATUS_LABELS and QualityReport::GROUPS are LocalisedLabels objects: they answer [], fetch, keys, each and to_h like the hashes they replace (so HeaReport and the views are unchanged) and look up netd.institution_status.<code> and netd.quality_groups.<code>.label/.description at each use. Dates on public pages are printed with l(time, format: :netd) (time.formats.netd and date.formats.netd in en.yml, same output as the earlier strftime). P4f: netd.admin holds the admin navigation and the sign-in, password, activity log, level review, problem report and CSV upload pages (admin_time uses l(..., format: :netd)); netd.mail.problem holds the problem-report mail, subject included (ProblemMailer calls I18n.t; the text template is not HTML-escaped, so its keys are plain and keep the label padding). Development and test set config.i18n.raise_on_missing_translations = true, so a key missing from en.yml fails at once there; production keeps the English fallback. P4g: netd.admin also holds the dashboard, source, record correction, duplicates, quality, usage and report-filter pages (dates through l(..., format: :netd), :netd_utc for the duplicates decisions, date.formats.netd for the usage days); UsageCount::EVENTS is a LocalisedLabels over netd.usage_events (the counting code reads only its codes); every flash message comes from netd.flash through ApplicationController#flash_text (private; plain keys, escaped by the layout). Text that stays in code: the contents of the reports for the regulator (HeaReport: titles, headings, notes, its GROUPS and COLUMNS labels, maintenance track), the problem types ProblemReport::PROBLEMS (stored as text in each report and validated against the list; translating them needs codes and a data migration, left to a release agreed with the maintenance track), model validation messages (errors.full_messages, the Harvester source checks), field names on the record correction page (humanize of the field code), and values from the data or the quality report (element labels, institution names, suggested improvements). Counts that need a plural use I18n's one/other keys with count: (browse.departments, replacing pluralize). Templates call nt('area.key', **values) (ApplicationHelper; components use helpers.nt), which adds Netd.text_values (portal, country, country_adjective, regulator, regulator_short, email, host, base_url) for interpolation. Each heading, paragraph, list item and table cell is one key (heading_html for the page heading, page_title for the browser title; other keys are named after their first words); a link inside a sentence is %{linkN} with its text in a plain key <key>_linkN. Sentences built around optional credits (About, Credits, For Institutions) are split into parts that the template joins. Project, members, contributors and publications stay data in publications.yml (its credits.hosting block was removed in P4b: the host comes from config/country.yml). Text that was written in the template is a _html key (output as written, interpolated values escaped); text that was a Ruby string passed to a helper is a plain key (escaped where shown), so that the escaping, and therefore the output, stays as before. regulator_link writes the regulator's linked name with the same attribute order as before. Line breaks inside a sentence are now single spaces: pages differ from the earlier ones in white space only. A second language is a copy of en.yml under its own code (production sets config.i18n.fallbacks = true, so a key missing from a translation falls back to English).
  • Theme (P5a): themes/<name>/ holds stylesheets/theme.css (the --netd-* and Bootstrap --bs-* custom properties, the wordmark font and its web-font import) and public/ (logos and other files). portal.theme in country.yml names it (Netd.theme, "default" when absent; Netd.theme_dir). The initializer netd_theme.rb stops start-up if theme.css is missing, adds stylesheets/ to the Propshaft asset paths (application.css imports theme.css last, so a theme can also override rules) and serves public/ with a second ActionDispatch::Static after the one for portal/public (same cache headers), so a credit's logo keeps its /images/<file> address. netd.css keeps the layout and reads every brand colour through the variables. Shipped: zambia (today's look) and default (neutral slate and blue, system serif wordmark, no logos). The release archive (access/release.sh) includes themes/.
  • Theme, second part (P5b): the site icons icon.png and icon.svg (used by the Rails application layout and the web app manifest) moved from portal/public to the theme's public/ (zambia: the same files; default: a neutral book icon); a file in portal/public would be served first, so none is left there. The browser-tab icon of the Blacklight pages comes from favicon_link_tag, which ApplicationHelper overrides: when the theme has public/favicon.svg or public/favicon.ico (Netd.theme_favicon) it links that file, otherwise it calls Blacklight's own (the zambia theme has none, so its pages are unchanged; default has favicon.svg). Netd.credit_logo(c) returns a credit's logo only when the file exists in the theme's public/images or in portal/public/images (looked up once per file name); without it, About and Credits show the credit's name (span.netd-credit-name, styled in netd.css) inside the same link, and the footer leaves the logo link out (the sentence beside it already names and links the credit).
  • Rendered files (P6a): robots.txt (the sitemap address) and the REST API specification (portal name, adjective, regulator, addresses, OAI identifier prefix, contact) are ERB templates in portal/app/views/static_files/ (robots.text.erb, openapi.text.erb) served by StaticFilesController (ActionController::Base: no layout, no usage counting) at /robots.txt and /api/v1/openapi.yaml with text/plain and text/yaml and one day's public caching; the contact is the developed by credit and the project address in publications.yml. They are no longer in portal/public, which is served before the routes; the initializer netd_static_files.rb warns at start-up if a copy is left there. The specification's example values (unza, University of Zambia) stay as examples. Changes to the API specification are now made in portal/app/views/static_files/openapi.text.erb (maintenance track).
  • Not yet configurable (later packaging releases): the problem types ProblemReport::PROBLEMS (stored as text in each report and would need codes first) and the reports for the regulator (HeaReport, maintenance track: English headings and strftime dates), the Apache sites and the operations scripts (P6), and the title-page word list (P9, a model change). The class HeaReport keeps its name (not visible to users; a rename would touch the maintenance track's report code for no visible gain).

docs.title: 9. Design rationale
docs.text: Decision Alternatives considered Reason Custom Python pipeline + Blacklight InvenioRDM; VuFind; DSpace as aggregator ML models are Python; the raw store makes cleaning re-runnable; InvenioRDM's harvester module is experimental and its "harvest always wins" policy overwrites cleaning; the server's RAM (3.8 GiB, shared) rules out an Invenio stack SQLite (v0.1) PostgreSQL Zero extra memory or daemon; adequate for ≤ 100k records; can migrate later dim before etdms/oai_dc oai_dc only Retains qualified DSpace fields (advisor, local fields) Set hierarchy for Faculty Manual mapping only UNZA RIMS ETD collections are Schools; derivable with provenance set: Provenance and confidence on every value Overwrite in place Lets the team measure each model's contribution; low-confidence values don't pollute facets Sub-path /beta New sub-domain No DNS change needed (constraint C3) Native systemd services Docker Lower memory overhead on a shared 4 GB server REST API v1 in Rails on ActionController::API, own representation and OpenAPI file Blacklight's .json views only; GraphQL; a separate API service .json exposes Solr field names and changes with the interface; GraphQL adds a dependency and is harder to cache and rate-limit; no new service or memory; the OpenAPI file gives clients a contract and generated documentation Admin panel inside the Rails portal, Rails 8 built-in authentication A separate admin application; Devise; HTTP basic authentication in Apache No new service or memory; one gem (bcrypt); sessions can be listed, expired and audited, unlike basic authentication; accounts from the command line keep the attack surface small OAI-PMH provider in Rails, reading Solr A separate OAI server (e.g. jOAI); serving from the SQLite store No extra service or memory; Solr already holds every exposed field; stateless tokens survive Puma restarts

docs.title: 10. Known limitations (v0.8)
docs.text:
• Supervisor and Department are empty in every source's harvested metadata; they are now filled from PDF front matter by the baseline model where its confidence reaches 0.8 (FR-14). Older UNZA ETDs are scanned and depend on OCR; about 15% of UNZA PDF links return HTTP 500 from the repository. UNILUS PDF links point to an internal address the portal cannot reach.
  • 30 of the 34 HEA-listed institutions show 0 (no reachable ETD repository).
  • HTTPS for netd.ac.zm is in place (NFR-9); HTTP redirects to HTTPS since v0.8.
  • The old portal's OAI-PMH endpoint (/OAI-PMH) is retired with it; NETD v2's own provider at /oai (EI-4) replaces it from release 0.18.
  • No deduplication (FR-19).
